items.headline: EIA: Southwest hydropower hit record low this summer, 19% below last year
items.take: EIA's Form EIA-923 data show Southwest hydropower generation from April through August 2026 was 19% lower than a year earlier and 28% lower than the 10-year average. Lake Powell reached 3,518 feet at the end of September versus a 3,490-foot minimum power pool, and Lake Mead reached 1,038 feet versus 950 feet. AlphaGen read: EIA's November STEO projects 6.13 billion kWh of Southwest hydropower in 2026, 24% below the 10-year average, and 2027 is forecast at 6.1 billion kWh, 0.5% below 2026.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy

items.headline: CFTC sues Arkansas over state action against Kalshi, its 11th state suit
items.take: The CFTC said Nov. 13 it filed a lawsuit to block Arkansas from halting event-contract trading and from imposing up to hundreds of millions of dollars in civil penalties on CFTC-registered exchanges. Arkansas is bringing a civil enforcement action against Kalshi in state court, and the CFTC calls Arkansas the 11th state it has sued. AlphaGen read: the agency has also filed amicus briefs in four federal Courts of Appeal and one state Supreme Court, so the federal-versus-state jurisdiction question is being argued in several courts at once.

items.headline: Virgin Galactic to exchange ~$12.5M of 2027 convertible notes for stock
items.take: In a Nov. 13 8-K, Virgin Galactic said it agreed to exchange approximately $12.5 million of its 2.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 for common shares, which would cut the outstanding 2027 notes from $17.9 million to $5.4 million. The exchange is expected to close on or about Nov. 19, subject to customary conditions, with the share count set over a two-day observation period beginning Nov. 17. AlphaGen read: the remaining $5.4 million is about 1.3% of the $425.0 million originally issued in January 2022.
items.source_name: SEC EDGAR, Virgin Galactic Holdings Form 8-K

items.headline: Virgin Galactic amends 9.80% first lien notes; will redeem 80% of asset-sale proceeds
items.take: Virgin Galactic said that on Nov. 13, with requisite holder consent and no consent fee, it amended the indenture for its 9.80% First Lien Notes due 2028 to permit certain asset sales without triggering a mandatory redemption. In return it agreed to redeem notes equal to 80% of net cash proceeds above $5 million from any such sale occurring by July 30, 2027, payable in cash or up to 2,230,425 shares. AlphaGen read: the notes' outstanding balance is $172.0 million versus $212.5 million at issuance in December 2025, and the filing says there is no assurance any asset sale will occur.
items.source_name: SEC EDGAR, Virgin Galactic Holdings Form 8-K

items.headline: Schnabel: ICT drove over a quarter of U.S. productivity gains with under 2% of jobs
items.take: ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said in her Nov. 13 Vilnius speech that since 2000 more than a quarter of total growth in U.S. value added per employee has accrued in the information and communications technology sector, which accounts for less than 2% of total employment. She said the typical American lives in a USD 45,000 economy, not a USD 67,000 one. AlphaGen read: she uses this to argue that standard U.S.-euro area GDP per capita comparisons overstate the gap in living standards.

items.headline: Schnabel: German real GDP per capita fell 0.5% in 2019-2024; export view a 'misdiagnosis'
items.take: ECB's Isabel Schnabel said Germany's real GDP per capita fell by 0.5% from 2019 to 2024, citing demographic change, energy costs that remain elevated compared with pre-pandemic levels, protectionism and global competition, especially from China. She said treating eroding export market shares as the main cause is a misdiagnosis, and that over the past ten years Germany's real goods exports have broadly tracked the global cycle. AlphaGen read: the speech contrasts Germany's weakness with growth in the euro area's south.

items.headline: Schnabel: Spain's renewables cut wholesale power prices; Ireland a tech and pharma hub
items.take: In her Nov. 13 speech, ECB's Isabel Schnabel said Spain has emerged as a European leader in renewable energy, which has significantly reduced wholesale electricity prices and the country's vulnerability to global energy price shocks. She said Ireland has become a global hotspot for technology, pharmaceutical and life science companies and has the highest share of tertiary students in natural sciences, mathematics and statistics fields in the EU. AlphaGen read: these are her country examples of structural change supporting growth.

items.headline: Project Meridian FX APAC: Partior built prototype; RBA, BSP observed; 3 reports out
items.take: The Bank of England, Monetary Authority of Singapore and Bank of Thailand said Partior, the project's delivery partner, developed, integrated and tested the Synchronisation Operator prototype for the trial. The Reserve Bank of Australia and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas participated as observer central banks, and the findings are published across three reports: Introduction and Executive Summary, Technical Report, and Policy Report. AlphaGen read: the release says future work could extend the approach to additional jurisdictions and a wider range of currencies.

items.headline: Barr: top 10% of households hold nearly three-fourths of U.S. wealth; lower half 2%
items.take: In a Nov. 12 speech at Yale, Governor Barr cited the Fed's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances: the wealthiest 10 percent of households hold nearly three-fourths of all wealth, the top 1 percent hold about one-third (nearly $60 trillion), and the lower half of households have only 2 percent. He said the top 10 percent by income receive almost one-half of all income. AlphaGen read: the survey shows wealth is more concentrated than income.

items.headline: Barr: labor share of national income hit record low 52.8% in Q2 2026
items.take: Governor Barr said the labor share of U.S. national income was fairly steady between 60 percent and 65 percent after World War II, began falling in 2001, and reached a record low of 52.8 percent in the second quarter of 2026. He cited three causes from economic research: technology that reduced labor demand, market power concentrated in a few firms, and weaker worker bargaining power. AlphaGen read: Barr uses the labor-share decline to frame how AI could affect income distribution.

items.headline: Barr: top-1% threshold household has 75x median wealth: $16.3M vs $215,000
items.take: Governor Barr said a household at the lower edge of the top 1 percent has 75 times the wealth of the median household, $16.3 million versus $215,000, and a household at the lower edge of the top 0.1 percent has 300 times as much. He added that 31 percent of respondents to the Fed's 2025 household economics survey lacked the cash to cover a $500 emergency expense. AlphaGen read: the speech pairs top-end wealth figures with a measure of everyday financial fragility.

items.headline: Schnabel: euro-area GDP per capita would be 21% higher on U.S. working hours
items.take: ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said a U.S. employee works around 40 more days a year than one in the euro area, and that matching U.S. hours, holding hourly productivity and the employment rate constant, would lift euro area real GDP per capita 21%, closing about two-thirds of the real income gap with the United States. She said the top 10% of U.S. earners take around 37% of after-tax national income versus around 27% in the euro area. AlphaGen read: she argues the headline income gap partly reflects work-time choices and distribution.

items.headline: Schnabel: southern euro-area economies now among Europe's fastest growing
items.take: In her Nov. 13 Vilnius speech, Schnabel said southern euro area countries, synonymous with crises and austerity a decade ago, are now among the fastest-growing economies in Europe, with record investment and declining unemployment. She said their financing conditions relative to Germany, despite some recent spread widening, remain close to their most favourable since 2008, and the European Commission projects Spain, Portugal and Greece potential growth above the euro area average. AlphaGen read: the speech frames the south as evidence that structural reform pays off.

items.headline: October PPI final demand +0.3%; goods +0.5%, services +0.2%
items.take: BLS reported the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3 percent in October, seasonally adjusted, and increased 6.5 percent unadjusted for the 12 months ended in October. Final demand goods rose 0.5 percent and final demand services moved up 0.2 percent, the fifth consecutive advance. AlphaGen read: producer-level price pressure is still building, led by goods.

items.headline: PPI less foods, energy, trade services +0.5% in October, same as September
items.take: BLS said the index for final demand less foods, energy, and trade services rose 0.5 percent in October, the same as in September, and advanced 4.9 percent over the 12 months ended in October. Margins for final demand trade services decreased 0.2 percent, and final demand energy edged down 0.1 percent while final demand foods increased 1.3 percent. AlphaGen read: the core measure is running above the headline's 0.3 percent, with trade margins and energy lower in the same report.

items.headline: PPI goods +0.5% after +2.5% in Sept; organic chemicals +3.9%, trucking +3.9%
items.take: BLS reported final demand goods increased 0.5 percent in October following a 2.5-percent rise in September, with basic organic chemicals up 3.9 percent; final demand goods rose 10.2 percent over the 12 months ended in October. Over 80 percent of the October increase in final demand services is attributable to truck transportation of freight, which rose 3.9 percent. AlphaGen read: freight and chemicals are the pressure points in this report.

items.headline: Fed sets 2027 payment-services prices: 1.4% average rise, higher check fees
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board announced pricing, effective Jan. 1, 2027, for Reserve Bank payment services including checks, ACH, instant payments and wholesale services. The Fed expects to recover 101.5 percent of actual and imputed expenses in 2027, with an estimated 1.4 percent average price increase for established, mature services. The Banks also announced check-service changes, including optimized processing windows during low-volume periods and higher fees for banks and credit unions; the release says consumers' and businesses' ability to pay with or receive checks is not affected. AlphaGen read: the changes fall on how banks process checks with the Reserve Banks, not on how households write them.

items.take: BEA said imports of goods rose $4.4 billion to $346.9 billion in September. Capital goods rose $11.6 billion, pharmaceutical preparations $2.9 billion and consumer goods $2.4 billion, while industrial supplies and materials fell $3.7 billion, nonmonetary gold $2.7 billion and crude oil $1.3 billion. AlphaGen read: the rise was concentrated in capital goods, with materials, gold and crude pulling the other way.

August imports of goods were also revised up $0.2 billion and imports of services up $0.4 billion. AlphaGen read: the revisions raised both sides of the August ledger by small amounts, and the release shows a revised August deficit of $105.7 billion.

items.headline: Barr: inequality is 'not immutable'; policy choices shaped its past swings
items.take: In a Nov. 12 speech, Governor Barr said that by many estimates today's inequality is among the highest in the past 100 years, narrowed in the decades after World War II, and began increasing again beginning in the late 1970s. He said the history suggests policy choices play a crucial role, alongside economic growth, technological change, education and globalization. AlphaGen read: Barr uses the historical record to frame how AI could affect the distribution of wealth and income.

items.headline: Moody's closes €500M 4.125% notes due 2033; proceeds may repay 2027 notes

Net proceeds are expected to be used for general corporate purposes, which may include repaying its 1.75% Senior Notes due 2027. AlphaGen read: the filing lists the 2027 notes as one possible use of proceeds, not a commitment.

items.headline: BoE, MAS and Bank of Thailand publish Project Meridian FX APAC findings
items.take: The three central banks said today their trial showed synchronised settlement can be achieved across central bank systems with different technologies, testing payment-versus-payment FX settlement and multilateral net FX across real-time gross settlement and distributed-ledger systems. The Bank of England said it plans to launch a live synchronisation interface in 2028. AlphaGen read: this is a test-environment result, and the release frames it as insight for developing a live service.
items.source_name: Bank of England, joint media release (13 Nov 2026)

items.headline: ECB's Schnabel: Europe lacks scale, not talent; backs a '28th regime'
items.take: In a Nov. 13 speech at the Bank of Lithuania's economics conference in Vilnius, ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said a 28th regime would give firms access to the entire European market and the scale to turn innovation into growth. She said that if Europeans worked as many hours as Americans, holding productivity per hour and the employment rate constant, euro area real GDP per capita would be 21% higher. AlphaGen read: the speech is about Europe's growth model and does not discuss interest rates.
items.source_name: European Central Bank, speech by Isabel Schnabel

items.take: BLS says real average hourly earnings for all employees were unchanged from September to October, seasonally adjusted, as a 0.4% rise in average hourly earnings matched a 0.4% rise in the CPI-U; real average weekly earnings were also unchanged. BLS adds that over-the-year comparisons are unavailable because October 2025 CPI data could not be collected during the late-2025 funding lapse. items.headline: EIA: U.S. imports of Venezuelan crude hit 701,000 b/d in July, most since 2017
items.take: EIA's Nov. 6 Today in Energy note says U.S. crude imports from Venezuela averaged 701,000 barrels per day in July 2026, the most since May 2017, before easing to 655,000 b/d in August; they started the year at 200,000 b/d. EIA attributes the rise to strong refinery demand amid high global refinery margins and eased U.S. restrictions on purchases from the country. AlphaGen read: Gulf Coast refiners configured for heavy sour crude are the main buyers EIA points to.

items.headline: EIA lifts November gas storage forecast by almost 70 Bcf; Henry Hub $2.87 Nov-Mar
items.take: EIA's Nov. 10 release says it expects almost 70 billion cubic feet more natural gas in U.S. storage at the end of November than it forecast in October, after a warm start to the month. The November STEO has Henry Hub spot averaging $2.87 per million Btu from November through March, 16% less over that period than last month's forecast, with more gas in storage throughout the winter. AlphaGen read: warmer weather and fuller storage are what lowered the winter price forecast.

items.headline: EIA expects record U.S. power-sector generation of almost 4,390 billion kWh in 2026
items.take: EIA's November outlook release expects U.S. electric power sector generation to reach a record of almost 4,390 billion kilowatthours in 2026, up 2.7% from 2025. It projects natural gas at 40% of generation in 2026 and 39% in 2027, solar at 8% in 2026 and 10% in 2027, and coal at 15% in both years. AlphaGen read: the generation mix is shifting toward solar while total demand for power keeps rising.
items.source_name: EIA, Press Release (11/10/2026): EIA raises November natural gas storage forecast after warm start to month

items.headline: EIA: U.S. commercial crude inventories fell to lowest October level since 2014
items.take: EIA's Nov. 10 release says U.S. commercial crude oil inventories fell to their lowest October level since 2014, and it expects U.S. crude production to reach a record 14.3 million barrels per day in 2027, up from 13.9 million in 2026. The release forecasts Brent spot averaging $86 a barrel in 2027. AlphaGen read: tight inventories and rising output are the two supply-side facts in EIA's forecast.

items.headline: September PPI: processed goods for intermediate demand +2.5%, 14.1% over 12 months
items.take: BLS says the index for processed goods for intermediate demand rose 2.5% in September, the largest rise since 2.8% in May, with more than 80% of the advance attributable to a 10.2% increase in processed energy goods. Nearly half of the rise traces to a 21.0% increase in diesel fuel, and the 12-month increase of 14.1% is the largest since 14.3% in August 2022. items.headline: September PPI: unprocessed intermediate goods +8.4%, crude petroleum +28.3%
items.take: BLS says prices for unprocessed goods for intermediate demand rose 8.4% in September, the largest increase since 9.2% in February 2022, and are up 21.5% for the 12 months ended in September. Over 80% of the September advance is attributable to unprocessed energy materials, which jumped 22.2%, led by a 28.3% rise in crude petroleum. AlphaGen read: this is the earliest stage of the PPI pipeline, and it shows the September price surge was concentrated in crude oil.

items.headline: September PPI: services for intermediate demand +0.9%, trade margins +2.0%
items.take: BLS says the index for services for intermediate demand rose 0.9% in September, matching the largest increase since 0.9% in April, with over 40% of the advance traced to a 2.0% jump in trade-services margins. Transportation and warehousing services rose 1.8%, and the index is up 6.3% over the 12 months ended in September, the largest 12-month advance since 6.3% in January 2023. AlphaGen read: business-to-business service prices, not just fuel, were climbing in the latest PPI (released Oct. 15).

items.take: BLS says the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 1.3% in September (seasonally adjusted) after 0.5% in August and 0.2% in July. On an unadjusted basis the index climbed 6.3% for the 12 months ended in September, the largest 12-month increase since 6.4% in December 2022. AlphaGen read: this September report, published Oct. 15, is the latest PPI in BLS's file and sets the bar the next report will be judged against.

items.headline: September PPI: final demand energy +10.8%; gasoline +20.3% drives half the goods rise
items.take: BLS says final demand goods prices rose 2.6% in September, the largest increase since the data were first calculated in December 2009, and more than 80% of the rise is attributable to final demand energy, which jumped 10.8%. Half of the goods increase traces to gasoline, up 20.3%, with diesel fuel, jet fuel, residential electric power and crude petroleum also higher. AlphaGen read: the producer-price surge in September was mainly an energy story.

items.headline: September PPI services +0.8%: trade margins +1.4%, transportation and warehousing +3.4%
items.take: BLS says final demand services prices rose 0.8% in September, the largest rise since a 0.8% gain in April. Nearly half of the increase is attributable to a 1.4% rise in margins for final demand trade services, while transportation and warehousing services rose 3.4% and services less trade, transportation and warehousing rose 0.3%. Margins for machinery and vehicle wholesaling advanced 3.9%, while margins for automotive fuels and lubricants retailing dropped 30.3%.

items.headline: September PPI excluding food, energy and trade +0.5%, 5.0% over 12 months; foods +1.2%
items.take: BLS says final demand less foods, energy and trade services rose 0.5% in September after 0.3% in August, and 5.0% for the 12 months ended in September. Final demand foods rose 1.2% and goods less foods and energy rose 0.3%, while chicken egg prices dropped 39.7%. AlphaGen read: the narrower measure also accelerated, so the September jump was not confined to energy.

items.headline: CPI owners' equivalent rent +0.3%, rent +0.2% in October; lodging away from home +0.6%
items.take: BLS says the shelter index rose 0.3% in October after 0.4% in September, with owners' equivalent rent up 0.3% and rent up 0.2%. Lodging away from home rose 0.6% after a 2.0% increase the previous month. AlphaGen read: the monthly shelter gain slowed from September, while lodging remains the volatile piece.

items.headline: CPI used cars and trucks -1.2% in October, -3.3% over 12 months; new vehicles +0.2%
items.take: BLS reports the used cars and trucks index fell 1.2% in October after rising 0.7% in September, and is down 3.3% over the 12 months ended October on an unadjusted basis. items.headline: CPI recreation index +0.8% in October after +0.5%; motor vehicle insurance +0.7%
items.take: BLS says the recreation index rose 0.8% in October after 0.5% in September, while motor vehicle insurance rose 0.7%, household furnishings and operations 0.2% and education 0.3%. items.headline: CPI gasoline +1.0% seasonally adjusted in October, but down 0.7% before adjustment

items.headline: Bowman: October CPI suggests 12-month core PCE inflation likely rose to 3.3%
items.take: In her Nov. 10 speech, Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman said the day's consumer price index suggests 12-month core PCE inflation likely moved up further to 3.3 percent in October, as upward pressures from higher energy prices and AI-related demand continue to flow through to core goods and services prices. She said progress on lowering inflation has stalled over the past two years or so and that the latest data suggest price pressures may be broadening. AlphaGen read: her own forecast still has core PCE moving closer to 2 percent next year, so the worry is persistence, not a changed endpoint.

items.headline: Bowman flags equity correction and sharp rise in long-term rates as growth risks
items.take: Bowman said she sees risks to economic activity originating in financial markets, including a large correction in equity valuations if returns on AI investment fall short of expectations and a sharp increase in private longer-term interest rates. She said lower equity prices could undermine resilience in consumer spending and higher rates could further strain interest-rate-sensitive sectors like housing and small business investment. AlphaGen read: she is naming the two channels, wealth effects and borrowing costs, that would link markets to the real economy.

items.headline: Waller: uncertainty since early 2025 may be holding back hiring; cites Beige Book
items.take: Governor Waller said hiring and job-switching may have been restrained by factors that have raised economic uncertainty since early 2025, including the advent of AI, tariffs, changes in immigration policy and enforcement, and general uncertainty about the outlook. He cited the Fed's November 2025 Beige Book, where employers reported hiring was unusually restrained because of uncertainty, and the most recent Beige Book, where several Districts reported firms delayed hiring or anticipate less job creation after investing in AI. He said he does not think uncertainty has diminished much since then. AlphaGen read: he is treating part of the low-hire pattern as uncertainty-driven rather than purely structural.

items.headline: Waller: low firing may partly reflect 2020-2023 job-switching surge, possibly temporary
items.take: Waller said low firing may be a consequence of the surge in job-switching from 2020 to 2023, since workers in new jobs are less inclined to change jobs again. He said that if this is a large factor it may be temporary, because workers stay in their jobs a median of three years before switching again and the last of the pandemic job switchers are nearing that threshold. AlphaGen read: this is the argument that labor-market dynamism could recover without a policy change.

items.take: In a Nov. 10 statement to the European Parliament's economic affairs committee, ECB Executive Board member Piero Cipollone said the Eurosystem's Pontes platform, launched in September, had 18 market participants and market DLT operators onboarded on day one. He said that on Nov. 2 it settled the European Stability Mechanism's first digitally native benchmark bond, of €1 billion. AlphaGen read: the ECB is presenting settlement of tokenised securities in central bank money as already operational, not a pilot.

items.headline: ECB: 36 payment providers chosen from 50+ applicants for digital euro pilot
items.take: Cipollone said in July the ECB announced the 36 payment service providers selected for the digital euro pilot from more than 50 applicants, covering banks and non-bank providers. He said a September call for online and mobile merchants will have its final selection announced early next year, and the next wave of innovation-platform activities, including conditional payments and AI in payments, runs from January to June 2027. AlphaGen read: the pilot is widening to remote payments before the legal framework is final.

items.headline: ECB's Lane: speeches between meetings can move rates across maturities
items.take: In a Nov. 10 keynote at the Bank of England and its Watchers Conference, ECB Executive Board member Philip Lane cited research on thousands of speeches, interviews and hearings showing that communication between policy meetings can affect market interest rates across maturities. He said it can help markets anticipate policy changes, particularly ahead of tightening episodes, and that its cumulative effect over time can be comparable to that of policy announcements, especially at longer maturities. AlphaGen read: for rate-watchers, the ECB is saying a speech calendar matters between meetings, not only decision days.

items.headline: ECB's Cipollone backs mandatory cash acceptance; euro notes turn 25 in two months
items.take: Cipollone told the European Parliament committee on Nov. 10 that the ECB supports strong legislative provisions on mandatory cash acceptance, access to cash across the euro area and the resilience of cash infrastructure. He said that in two months the 25th anniversary of euro banknotes and coins entering circulation will be marked, and that adoption of the legal framework is necessary to issue a digital euro. AlphaGen read: the ECB is pairing its digital euro push with a cash-protection message to win legislative support.

items.headline: Waller expects Q4 GDP growth to back off as spending aligns with income and wealth
items.take: In a Nov. 10 speech, Fed Governor Waller said the initial estimate was that real GDP rose 3.4 percent in the third quarter, with consumption 'helped by a booming stock market' and business investment continuing to surge, especially in high-tech equipment tied to the AI buildout. He said he expects growth to back off a bit in the current quarter as consumer spending slows to levels he thinks are more consistent with household income and wealth, while output keeps growing at a solid pace. AlphaGen read: his case for a slower fourth quarter rests on spending normalizing, not on a weakening labor market.

items.headline: Average private workweek holds at 34.4 hours in October; manufacturing 40.5, overtime 3.1
items.take: BLS reported that the average workweek for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls was unchanged at 34.4 hours in October. In manufacturing the workweek was unchanged at 40.5 hours and overtime edged up 0.1 hour to 3.1 hours, while the workweek for production and nonsupervisory employees declined 0.1 hour to 33.8 hours. AlphaGen read: hours were flat even as payrolls rose 165,000, so October's gain did not come from longer schedules.

items.headline: Health care added 42,000 jobs in October vs 31,000 average; hospitals +16,000
items.take: BLS said health care employment rose 42,000 in October, above its average monthly gain of 31,000 over the prior 12 months. Gains were in hospitals (+16,000), home health care services (+11,000) and outpatient care centers (+5,000). AlphaGen read: health care remains one of the three industries BLS named as driving October's 165,000 total, alongside professional and business services and transportation and warehousing.

items.headline: Waller: aging, education explain part of low dynamism; degree share 28% to 37%
items.take: Waller said part of the decline in both hiring and firing may reflect longer-run trends that predate the pandemic: an aging workforce, since older workers switch jobs less often, and rising education, since the share of adults 25 and older with at least a bachelor's degree has increased from 28 percent in 2010 to 37 percent. He said that if those were the only reasons, dynamism would be at a level consistent with trend, with no implications for monetary policy, but said that even after accounting for them, dynamism still seems somewhat low. AlphaGen read: the speech separates structural drift from cyclical weakness, which is the distinction that matters for policy.

items.headline: ECB: banknote design survey drew almost 10 million responses; first new notes early 2030s
items.take: ECB Executive Board member Piero Cipollone said the July survey on ten shortlisted designs for new euro banknotes, themed 'European culture' and 'Rivers and birds', received almost 10 million responses across all euro area countries and age groups. The Governing Council's decision on the final design concept is expected around the end of this year, when the survey results will also be published, and the first denominations of the new series are expected to enter circulation in the early 2030s. AlphaGen read: the timeline is slow, and the ECB paired it with support for mandatory cash acceptance rules.

items.headline: Take-Two fiscal Q2 revenue $1.50B vs $1.77B; net loss $54.0M, $0.29 a share
items.take: Take-Two's release for the three months ended Sept. 30, 2026 reported GAAP net revenue of $1,497.0 million versus $1,773.8 million a year earlier (-15.6% by AlphaGen's calculation) and a GAAP net loss of $54.0 million, or $0.29 per share, versus $0.73 per share. Total Net Bookings decreased 18% to $1.60 billion from $1.96 billion. AlphaGen read: the quarter's bookings and revenue both fell year over year, so the company's fiscal outlook rests on what comes after the quarter.
items.source_name: Take-Two Interactive Q2 FY2027 earnings release (SEC EX-99.1)

items.headline: Take-Two reiterates $8.0-$8.2B fiscal 2027 Net Bookings; Q3 guide $3.35-$3.50B
items.take: Take-Two's release reiterated an outlook for fiscal 2027 Net Bookings of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion and guided fiscal Q3 (quarter ending Dec. 31, 2026) Net Bookings to $3.35 billion to $3.50 billion and total net revenue to $3.27 billion to $3.42 billion. Its product table lists Grand Theft Auto VI for Nov. 19, 2026 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. AlphaGen read: the guidance step-up from the Sept. quarter's $1.60 billion of bookings to the Dec. quarter range is the figure to watch.
items.source_name: Take-Two Interactive Q2 FY2027 earnings release (SEC EX-99.1)

items.headline: Occidental Q3 EPS $1.61 vs $0.65; principal debt cut $1.8B to $10.0B
items.take: Occidental's third-quarter 2026 release, dated Nov. 9, reported diluted EPS of $1.61 versus $0.65 in Q3 2025 and net income attributable to common stockholders of $1,637 million versus $661 million. Adjusted EPS from continuing operations was $1.91 versus $0.51. The company said it reduced principal debt by $1.8 billion to $10.0 billion. AlphaGen read: both reported and adjusted earnings rose year over year while balance-sheet debt reduction continued.

items.headline: Occidental: Q3 operating cash flow $4.1B, production 1,427 Mboed, WTI avg $85.79
items.take: Occidental reported $4.1 billion of operating cash flow from continuing operations and $2.8 billion of free cash flow before working capital in Q3 2026, with $1.3 billion of capital spending. Global production was 1,427 Mboed, and the release gives a Q3 average WTI price of $85.79 per barrel. AlphaGen read: the release ties the quarter's cash generation to a Q3 WTI average well above $80.

items.headline: Lucid Q3 revenue $350.3M, up 4%; free cash flow consumption down 30% to $1.04B
items.take: Lucid's Q3 2026 release reported revenue of $350.3 million versus $336.6 million a year earlier, up 4%. Free cash flow consumption fell 30% sequentially to $1.04 billion, and total liquidity was $2.0 billion, or $3.75 billion pro forma for a $1.75 billion DDTL increase with PIF. The company said that liquidity is expected to fund operations and key investments into Q4 2027. AlphaGen read: revenue grew modestly while the release's focus is on cash burn and runway.
items.source_name: Lucid Group Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC EX-99.1)

items.headline: Q3 consumer spending: health care and restaurants led services; drugs led goods
items.take: BEA's advance Q3 estimate said the rise in consumer spending reflected increases in both services and goods. Within services, the increase was led by health care (mainly hospitals and outpatient services) and by food services and accommodations (mainly purchased meals and beverages); within goods, it was led by other nondurable goods (mainly prescription drugs). AlphaGen read: BEA's named drivers of the spending gain span health care, dining and prescription drugs.

items.headline: BEA: Q3 export decline led by petroleum; capital goods the largest import contributor
items.take: BEA said the third-quarter decrease in exports primarily reflected a decrease in goods, led by petroleum and related products, while the largest contributor to the increase in imports was capital goods other than automotive. Imports are a subtraction in the GDP calculation. AlphaGen read: BEA points to petroleum products as the lead factor in the export decline and to capital goods on the import side.

items.headline: September personal income +$54.5B, led by wages and Medicare benefits; outlays +$113.0B
items.take: BEA reported personal income rose $54.5 billion (0.2 percent) in September, primarily reflecting increases in compensation and government social benefits. Within compensation the increase was led by private wages and salaries; the social benefits increase was led by Medicare. Personal outlays rose $113.0 billion, more than twice the income gain. AlphaGen read: spending grew faster than income in dollar terms, consistent with the 3.8 percent saving rate BEA reported.

items.headline: ECB's Lane: new inflation target reached only about one in ten consumers
items.take: In a Nov. 10 speech, ECB Executive Board member Philip Lane cited research presented in the 2021 strategy review suggesting information about the new inflation target reached only around one in ten consumers in the months after its announcement, with most learning of it through television, radio and newspapers rather than directly from the ECB. He added that households and firms pay more attention to inflation when it is high and less when it is low and stable. AlphaGen read: the ECB is framing communication as something to tailor to the inflation backdrop.

items.headline: September PCE prices +0.5%, core +0.3%; 12-month rate 3.6%, core 3.1%
items.take: BEA's September release (Oct. 29) showed the PCE price index up 0.5 percent from August, versus 0.3 percent in August, with the index excluding food and energy up 0.3 percent in both months. From a year earlier, the PCE price index rose 3.6 percent and the core index 3.1 percent. AlphaGen read: headline PCE inflation ran above the core measure in September; BEA's next release is due Nov. 25.

items.headline: Q3 GDP: PCE price index 2.1% annualized vs 5.0% in Q2; core 2.5% vs 3.3%
items.take: BEA's advance estimate for the third quarter put the PCE price index up 2.1 percent at an annual rate, after 5.0 percent in the second quarter, and the index excluding food and energy up 2.5 percent, after 3.3 percent. The gross domestic purchases price index rose 3.0 percent versus 5.6 percent in Q2, and real final sales to private domestic purchasers increased 4.9 percent. AlphaGen read: quarterly price pressure slowed sharply from Q2 even as private demand stayed firm.

items.headline: BEA: lower Strategic Petroleum Reserve sales added to Q3 federal consumption
items.take: BEA said the Q3 pattern of nondefense federal spending primarily reflected crude oil sales from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which were smaller than in the second quarter and so raised government consumption expenditures. BEA noted the oil sold is reflected in other GDP components, so there is no direct effect on GDP. AlphaGen read: an energy-policy accounting detail that explains part of the government contribution to Q3 growth.

items.headline: CPI core goods +0.2%, services less energy +0.3% in October
items.take: BLS reported commodities less food and energy rose 0.2 percent in October after 0.3 percent in September, while services less energy services rose 0.3 percent after 0.4 percent. New vehicles rose 0.2 percent and apparel 0.1 percent, while used cars and trucks fell 1.2 percent. AlphaGen read: the 0.3 percent core CPI gain in October was split between modest goods and services increases.

items.headline: CPI electricity +0.9% in October; utility gas service -0.8%
items.take: BLS reported the electricity index rose 0.9 percent in October after 0.2 percent in September, while utility (piped) gas service fell 0.8 percent after a 0.3 percent decline. Energy services overall rose 0.6 percent, and the gasoline index rose 1.0 percent. AlphaGen read: household power bills moved higher in October while natural gas service costs eased.

items.headline: Sept imports of goods $346.9B: capital goods +$11.6B, computers +$7.6B
items.take: BEA and Census reported imports of goods rose $4.4 billion to $346.9 billion in September, led by capital goods (+$11.6 billion), including computers (+$7.6 billion) and computer accessories (+$5.7 billion), while semiconductors fell $1.2 billion. Industrial supplies and materials decreased $3.7 billion and crude oil imports fell $1.3 billion. AlphaGen read: the import increase was concentrated in computing equipment, consistent with the equipment investment BEA cited in third-quarter GDP.
items.source_name: BEA/Census, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026

items.headline: Three-month average trade deficit $101.2B, up $11.3B; services surplus $30.9B
items.take: BEA reported the average goods and services deficit increased $11.3 billion to $101.2 billion for the three months ending in September, $36.5 billion wider than the three months ending September 2025. Average exports rose $1.4 billion to $316.0 billion and average imports rose $12.7 billion to $417.2 billion. In September alone the goods deficit was $135.9 billion against a services surplus of $30.9 billion. The single-month narrowing to $105.0 billion sits inside a wider three-month trend.
items.source_name: BEA/Census, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026

items.headline: Sept goods deficits: Mexico $28.7B, Vietnam $25.3B, Taiwan $21.9B, China $17.9B
items.take: On a Census basis, the U.S. goods deficit in September was largest with Mexico ($28.7 billion), followed by Vietnam ($25.3 billion), Taiwan ($21.9 billion), China ($17.9 billion) and the European Union ($14.2 billion). Surpluses were recorded with the Netherlands ($7.7 billion), South and Central America ($6.2 billion) and the United Kingdom ($3.0 billion). Taiwan and Vietnam ranking above China in the monthly deficit table is a notable feature of the September data.
items.source_name: BEA/Census, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026

items.headline: CPI transportation services +0.8% in October after +0.6% in September
items.take: BLS data show the transportation services index rose 0.8% in October, following gains of 0.6% in September and 0.5% in August, while the broader services-less-energy-services index rose 0.3% in October. Within the release, motor vehicle insurance rose 0.7% and airline fares increased. Used cars and trucks fell 1.2%, while core rose 0.3%. AlphaGen read: the transportation services monthly change has risen in each of the last three months.
items.source_name: BLS, Consumer Price Index Summary, October 2026

items.headline: CPI fuel oil +2.0% in October after +15.3%; energy commodities +0.8%
items.take: BLS reported the fuel oil index rose 2.0% in October after a 15.3% jump in September, and energy commodities rose 0.8% after 9.3%. Electricity rose 0.9% and utility (piped) gas service fell 0.8%, leaving energy services up 0.6%. AlphaGen read: October's energy gains were far smaller than September's, but fuel oil and electricity still rose.
items.source_name: BLS, Consumer Price Index Summary, October 2026

items.headline: Sept consumer spending +$113.1B: services +$78.1B, goods +$35.1B
items.take: BEA reported current-dollar personal consumption expenditures rose $113.1 billion (0.5%) in September, reflecting a $78.1 billion increase in spending on services and a $35.1 billion increase in spending on goods. Real PCE rose $2.6 billion (less than 0.1%), because the PCE price index rose 0.5% in the month. AlphaGen read: most of the dollar increase in spending was services, and nearly all of the increase was price rather than volume.
items.source_name: BEA, Personal Income and Outlays, September 2026

items.headline: Transportation jobs +104,000 since February; professional services +269,000 since Oct. 2025
items.take: BLS said transportation and warehousing has added 104,000 jobs since a recent employment low in February, with couriers and messengers (+71,000) contributing most of the gain, after +25,000 in October. Professional and business services has added 269,000 jobs since a recent low in October 2025, including +70,000 in October versus an average monthly gain of 15,000 over the prior 12 months. Total nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 in October against a 48,000 monthly average over the prior 12 months.

items.headline: Manufacturing jobs +19,000 in October, +101,000 since December 2025 low
items.take: BLS reported manufacturing employment continued to trend up in October (+19,000) and has increased by 101,000 since a recent low in December 2025, with gains in computer and electronic products (+7,000), machinery (+4,000) and primary metals (+4,000). The manufacturing average workweek was unchanged at 40.5 hours and overtime edged up 0.1 hour to 3.1 hours. AlphaGen read: manufacturing has added jobs in recent months, a counterpoint to the 165,000 total gain led by professional services.

items.headline: Unemployment rate holds 4.1%, in 4.1%-4.3% range since March; teens at 13.9%
items.take: BLS said the unemployment rate has remained in a narrow range of 4.1% to 4.3% since March. In October, rates showed little or no change for adult men (3.9%), adult women (3.6%), teenagers (13.9%), and people who are White (3.7%), Black (6.6%), Asian (2.8%) or Hispanic (4.7%). AlphaGen read: the stability of the headline rate masks wide gaps between groups.

items.headline: 6.0M outside labor force want a job; discouraged workers 448,000
items.take: BLS reported the number of people not in the labor force who currently want a job changed little at 6.0 million in October. Of those, the marginally attached were little changed at 1.6 million, and discouraged workers, a subset who believed no jobs were available for them, were little changed at 448,000. AlphaGen read: these groups sit outside the 4.1% unemployment rate but show slack that the headline does not count.

items.headline: CPI food: beef +0.9%, snacks +1.0% in October; beverages -0.3%
items.take: BLS reported the food index rose 0.5% in October after being unchanged in September. Within groceries, other food at home rose 0.7% as snacks rose 1.0%, meats, poultry, fish and eggs rose 0.5% with beef up 0.9%, and fruits and vegetables and dairy each rose 0.6%, while nonalcoholic beverages fell 0.3% and cereals and bakery products were unchanged. Full service meals rose 0.7% and limited service meals 0.4%. AlphaGen read: four of the six major grocery groups rose in October, per BLS, while one fell.

items.headline: CPI medical care +0.3% in October; hospital services +0.8%
items.take: BLS reported the medical care index rose 0.3% in October after 0.1% in September. Hospital services rose 0.8%, physicians' services 0.4% and prescription drugs 0.3%. AlphaGen read: hospital services rose the most of the three medical components BLS listed.

items.headline: CPI-U index 337.511, CPI-W 331.147 in October; November CPI due Dec. 10
items.take: BLS reported the CPI-U rose to an index level of 337.511 (1982-84=100), up 0.2% before seasonal adjustment, and the CPI-W rose to 331.147, up 0.1%. The chained CPI-U increased 0.2% not seasonally adjusted. BLS scheduled the November CPI for Thursday, December 10, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET.

items.headline: Part-time for economic reasons rises 339,000 to 4.8M in October
items.take: BLS reported the number of people employed part time for economic reasons increased by 339,000 to 4.8 million in October; these are people who would have preferred full-time work but had hours cut or could not find full-time jobs. The same release shows the unemployment rate at 4.1% and 7.1 million unemployed, both little changed. AlphaGen read: a headline jobless rate that holds steady can sit alongside a rise in involuntary part-time work.

items.headline: Payrolls: professional services +70,000, health care +42,000, transport +25,000
items.take: BLS said total nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 in October versus an average monthly gain of 48,000 over the prior 12 months. Professional and business services added 70,000 (prior 12-month average 15,000), health care 42,000 (average 31,000) and transportation and warehousing 25,000. AlphaGen read: the October gain was concentrated in a few sectors, with professional services the standout against its own trend.

items.headline: Long-term unemployed 2.0M, 27.6% of the jobless; participation 61.9%
items.take: BLS reported 2.0 million people jobless for 27 weeks or more in October, 27.6% of all unemployed people, little changed over the month. The labor force participation rate was 61.9% and the employment-population ratio 59.3%, both little changed, and BLS said the unemployment rate has stayed between 4.1% and 4.3% since March. AlphaGen read: a stable rate with a sizeable long-duration share is the backdrop for Fed talk of a low-hire labor market.

items.headline: Production workers' real hourly pay +0.1% in October; real weekly pay -0.3%
items.take: BLS said real average hourly earnings for production and nonsupervisory employees rose 0.1% from September to October (earnings +0.4%, CPI-W +0.3%), while real average weekly earnings fell 0.3% because the average workweek also fell 0.3%. For all employees, real hourly earnings were unchanged. AlphaGen read: for hourly and nonsupervisory workers, a shorter workweek more than offset the small hourly gain.

items.headline: Mortgage rate sits 2.34 points above 10-year yield: 7.18% vs 4.84% on Nov. 5
items.take: FRED data show the 30-year fixed mortgage rate (Freddie Mac weekly average) at 7.18% for the week of Nov. 5, down from 7.40% on Oct. 15 and 7.28% on Oct. 1, while the 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield was 4.84% on Nov. 5. The gap between them was 2.34 percentage points that day. AlphaGen read: the mortgage rate has eased over the past month, but it still carries a spread of more than two points over the 10-year Treasury.
items.source_name: FRED (Freddie Mac PMMS; Federal Reserve H.15)

items.headline: Brent-WTI gap narrows to $7.39 on Nov. 3 from $19.73 on Oct. 27
items.take: FRED daily spot data show Brent at $107.03 a barrel and WTI at $99.64 on Nov. 3, a gap of $7.39; on Oct. 27 Brent was $123.10 and WTI $103.37, a gap of $19.73. Brent fell $16.07 over that span while WTI fell $3.73. AlphaGen read: most of the narrowing came from a larger decline in Brent than in WTI.

items.headline: Richmond Fed's Barkin: demand healthy, inflation elevated, policy should move 'with care'
items.take: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said on Nov. 9 in Greer, S.C., that September PCE inflation was 3.6% headline and 3.1% core and that the unemployment rate was 4.1% in October; both figures match BEA and BLS releases. He described demand as healthy and inflation as stubbornly elevated, said the direction of policy is relatively straightforward but risks to demand are easy to envision, and said policy should move with care, speaking for himself and not the FOMC. AlphaGen read: another regional Fed president putting inflation, not the labor market, as the nearer-term risk.

items.headline: 5-year breakeven inflation rate 2.25% on Nov. 10, from 2.46% on Oct. 30
items.take: The 5-year breakeven inflation rate was 2.25% on Nov. 10, unchanged from Nov. 9 and down from 2.46% on Oct. 30, a 0.21 percentage-point decline, per FRED. AlphaGen read: the market-implied five-year inflation compensation has fallen over the last two weeks; the 10-year breakeven was 2.20% on Nov. 10.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (T5YIE)

items.headline: 3-month Treasury yield 4.24% on Nov. 9, from 4.17% on Nov. 5
items.take: The 3-month Treasury constant-maturity yield was 4.24% on Nov. 9, up from 4.17% on Nov. 5 and 4.19% on Nov. 6, per FRED. The effective federal funds rate was 3.88% over the same stretch, inside the 3.75%-4.00% target range. AlphaGen read: the 3-month yield sits 0.36 point above the effective funds rate.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DGS3MO, DFF)

items.headline: Chicago Fed financial conditions index -0.459 for week of Oct. 30, from -0.532 on Sept. 11
items.take: The Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index was -0.459 for the week ended Oct. 30, up from -0.467 the prior week and -0.532 for the week ended Sept. 11, per FRED. The index rose in each of the last eight weekly readings. AlphaGen read: the gauge has drifted higher, in the same direction as Governor Bowman's remark that conditions tightened a bit.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (NFCI)

items.headline: Yen 158.23 per dollar, sterling $1.3371 on Nov. 6; sterling down from $1.3483
items.take: The yen was 158.23 per U.S. dollar on Nov. 6, from 157.76 on Nov. 5 and 157.47 on Oct. 30, per FRED. The British pound was $1.3371 on Nov. 6, down from $1.3483 on Nov. 5, and the Chinese yuan was 6.6760 per dollar, from 6.6538 on Oct. 30. AlphaGen read: the dollar firmed against all three on the day.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DEXJPUS, DEXUSUK, DEXCHUS)

items.headline: ECB deposit facility rate 2.50% on Nov. 10; Fed funds target range 3.75%-4.00%
items.take: The ECB deposit facility rate was 2.50% on Nov. 10, and the Fed's target range was 3.75% to 4.00% with an effective funds rate of 3.88% on Nov. 9, per FRED. The gap between the Fed funds effective rate and the ECB deposit rate is 1.38 percentage points. AlphaGen read: the Fed target range sits 1.25 to 1.50 points above the ECB deposit rate.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (ECBDFR, DFEDTARL, DFEDTARU, DFF)

items.headline: Bank reserves $2.930T on Nov. 4, up $36.3B in a week; Treasury cash $957.2B
items.take: Reserve balances with Federal Reserve Banks were $2,930.1 billion on Nov. 4, up $36.3 billion from $2,893.8 billion on Oct. 28, per FRED. The Treasury General Account fell $42.6 billion to $957.2 billion over the same week. AlphaGen read: lower Treasury cash balances coincided with higher reserves.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (WRESBAL, WTREGEN)

items.headline: UK 10-year yield averaged 5.24% in September, Germany 3.47%, both up from August
items.take: FRED's OECD-sourced monthly long-term government bond yield series shows the United Kingdom at 5.2421% in September 2026, up from 4.9886% in August, and Germany at 3.4695%, up from 3.1857%. That is increases of about 25 and 28 basis points. AlphaGen read: both markets saw yields rise through the third quarter.

items.headline: Existing-home sales 3.99M annual rate in September, up from 3.93M in August
items.take: FRED's existing home sales series stood at 3.99 million at a seasonally adjusted annual rate in September 2026, up from 3.93 million in August and down from 4.08 million in September 2025. July was 4.06 million. AlphaGen read: sales ticked up in September but remain below the year-earlier pace.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (EXHOSLUSM495S)

items.headline: Case-Shiller national home price index 336.741 in August, up 2.1% from a year earlier
items.take: FRED's national Case-Shiller index (not seasonally adjusted) was 336.741 for August 2026, versus 337.262 in July, a 0.15% monthly decline, and 329.844 in August 2025, a 2.09% annual gain. AlphaGen read: annual price growth remains positive but the latest monthly reading slipped.

items.take: FRED's series for the Federal Reserve's Senior Loan Officer survey shows a net 1.7% of domestic banks tightening standards on commercial and industrial loans to large and middle-market firms in the October 2026 reading, versus 0.0 in July and 8.1 in April. AlphaGen read: the net share tightening remains small, and is below the April reading.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DRTSCILM)

items.take: ICE BofA option-adjusted spreads on FRED were 1.13 points for BBB-rated and 2.00 points for BB-rated U.S. corporate bonds on Nov. 9, versus 1.16 and 2.13 on Nov. 5. The all-investment-grade index spread was 0.91 on Nov. 9, from 0.93 on Nov. 5. AlphaGen read: spreads narrowed across these three indexes between Nov. 5 and Nov. 9.
