items.headline: U.S. regular gasoline averages $3.995 a gallon in week of Nov. 9, from $4.153
items.take: The weekly U.S. regular gasoline price was $3.995 per gallon on Nov. 9, down from $4.153 on Nov. 2 and $4.269 on Oct. 26, per FRED. That is a decline of $0.274 over two weeks. AlphaGen read: pump prices fell over the same stretch in which FRED shows Brent spot lower.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (GASREGW)

items.headline: Bowman: AI buildout pushing up prices of specific high-tech capital as supply is inelastic
items.take: Bowman said Nov. 10 that inflation pressures tied to the AI buildout seem to persist despite some early signs of slowing, because the buildout has quickly shifted investment demand toward specific types of high-tech capital while near-term supply is relatively inelastic. She said she mostly views these pressures as relative price shocks in specific sectors, and that over time increased AI adoption should raise productivity and put some downward pressure on inflation. AlphaGen read: the Fed is treating AI as both a near-term price pressure and a longer-term disinflation argument.

items.headline: Bowman: Brent topped $110 in late October; gasoline, diesel, jet fuel near spring highs
items.take: Bowman said Nov. 10 that Brent oil prices moved up to and above $110 per barrel in the second half of October before dropping sharply last week on optimism about a U.S.-Iran agreement after the midterm elections. She said gasoline, diesel and jet fuel prices moved up to near or even above their spring highs, reflecting both higher crude prices and wider refining margins. Her framing ties pump and fuel costs to refining spreads as well as crude, so a crude decline may not pass through fully.

items.headline: Bowman: Q3 GDP likely above 3%, but higher mortgage rates drag on home construction
items.take: Bowman said Nov. 10 that real GDP rose 2.4 percent in the first half of 2026 and likely grew at more than 3 percent in the third quarter, versus a 2 percent pace last year, helped by AI-related capital expenditures and solid consumer spending. She said some interest-rate-sensitive sectors such as residential investment have declined and that the recent rise in mortgage rates appears to be dragging home construction and sales down further. Growth is being carried by investment and spending while housing is the visible weak spot.

items.headline: Bowman: wage growth 3.1%, long-term unemployed share up in 'low-dynamism' labor market
items.take: Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said Nov. 10 that the wages and salaries component of the employment cost index rose 3.1 percent over 12 months in September, the same pace as average hourly earnings in October, and that the share of multiple job holders is back to early-2025 levels. She said the share of long-term unemployed workers has moved up significantly, but that layoffs have declined this year, offsetting weak hiring. The mix of slower wages and stable unemployment supports her view that the labor market is stable but not tight.

items.headline: Bowman: tariffs, energy, AI each ~one-fourth of above-target core PCE inflation
items.take: Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said on Nov. 10 that tariffs, energy and AI-related price pressures each accounted for roughly one-fourth of above-target core PCE inflation over the 12 months ending in September, with the remaining one-fourth likely reflecting persistent effects of inflationary shocks in recent years. She forecast core PCE inflation moving closer to 2 percent next year as those shocks wane or unwind. The split shows how much of the overshoot she attributes to sector-specific supply shocks rather than labor-market tightness.

items.headline: Bowman: financial conditions tightened a bit on equities, private rates, dollar
items.take: Bowman said financial conditions have tightened a bit recently because of lower equity prices, higher private interest rates and a stronger dollar, against a backdrop of increased market volatility. She said corporate bond and mortgage rate spreads have widened and tech-sector equity valuations have dropped as investors reassess expected returns and risks tied to external financing of AI investment. She listed a large equity correction and a sharp increase in private longer-term rates among the risks to economic activity.

items.headline: Bowman: Hormuz carried ~20% of global oil supply pre-conflict; freight costs surge
items.take: Bowman said the Strait of Hormuz accounted for about 20 percent of global oil supply before the Middle East conflict, roughly equivalent to total U.S. oil consumption. She said crude flows in the Persian Gulf have recovered to near pre-conflict levels, but freight rates and insurance premiums have surged, raising the cost of delivered oil, and that Brent dropped sharply last week on optimism about a U.S.-Iran agreement after the midterm elections. She expects energy-related price pressure to unwind when the conflict resolves, which keeps oil central to the Fed's inflation debate.

items.headline: Personal saving rate 3.8% in September as real disposable income falls 0.3%
items.take: BEA reported September personal saving was $911.1 billion, a personal saving rate of 3.8 percent of disposable income. Current-dollar disposable income rose 0.2 percent while real disposable income fell 0.3 percent, and real PCE rose less than 0.1 percent after 0.5 percent in August. With real income shrinking while spending still rose in dollar terms, households were working with a thin saving rate.

items.headline: Q3 GDP: inventories and equipment led investment; exports fell, imports rose
items.take: BEA's advance estimate put Q3 real GDP growth at a 3.4 percent annual rate and current-dollar GDP at 5.6 percent, with the gross domestic purchases price index up 3.0 percent. Investment, consumer spending and government spending contributed, partly offset by a decrease in exports, while imports increased. BEA said the investment increase primarily reflected private inventory investment, led by wholesale trade and manufacturing, and equipment, led by information processing equipment; the second estimate is due Nov. 25.

items.headline: BLS: Q3 productivity up 3.6%, unit labor costs down 0.7% (annualized)
items.take: BLS reported on Nov. 5 that productivity increased 3.6 percent in the third quarter of 2026 while unit labor costs decreased 0.7 percent, both at annualized rates. Faster output per hour alongside falling labor cost per unit points away from the labor side as a source of current inflation pressure, a theme Bowman also made on Nov. 10.

items.headline: Elevance reaffirms 2026 EPS of at least $22.00 and 90.2% benefit expense ratio
items.take: In a Nov. 10 Form 8-K (Item 7.01), Elevance Health said officers will speak with investors and analysts this week and reaffirm full-year 2026 shareholders' earnings guidance of at least $22.00 per diluted share, including about $7.00 of net unfavorable items. Adjusted shareholders' earnings are still expected at $29.00 or more per diluted share, and the benefit expense ratio at 90.2% plus or minus 50 basis points. The filing restates existing guidance rather than changing it.

items.headline: 10s-2s Treasury spread 0.25 point on Nov. 10, from 0.32 on Nov. 9
items.take: FRED data show the 10-year minus 2-year Treasury constant-maturity spread at 0.25 percentage point on Nov. 10, down from 0.32 on Nov. 9 and 0.38 on Nov. 5. The Nov. 10 reading is the lowest in the six observations from Nov. 3. The outright 10-year and 2-year yields for Nov. 10 were not yet in the series, so the move's source cannot be split between the two.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (T10Y2Y)

items.headline: 10-year breakeven inflation rate 2.20% on Nov. 10, from 2.30% on Nov. 3
items.take: FRED data show the 10-year breakeven inflation rate at 2.20% on Nov. 10, down from 2.22% on Nov. 9 and 2.30% on Nov. 3. That is a 10-basis-point decline over the six observations, with each reading below the prior day's from Nov. 4 through Nov. 10. The breakeven is the gap between nominal and inflation-indexed 10-year yields, so it reflects what the bond market prices for inflation compensation.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (T10YIE)

items.headline: Dollar General director Timothy McGuire to resign from board effective Dec. 3
items.take: In a Form 8-K (Item 5.02) filed Nov. 10, Dollar General said director Timothy I. McGuire notified the company on Nov. 5 of his decision to resign from the board for personal reasons, effective Dec. 3, 2026. The filing states his decision is not due to any disagreement with the company on any matter relating to its operations, policies or practices.

items.headline: September trade deficit narrows to $105.0B as exports rise to $321.5B
items.take: BEA and Census reported the September goods and services deficit at $105.0 billion, down $0.7 billion from a revised $105.7 billion in August. Exports were $321.5 billion and imports $426.6 billion; the year-to-date deficit is down $92.4 billion, or 12.2 percent, from the same period in 2025. The report was released Nov. 4, and the next one, covering October, is due Dec. 8.
items.source_name: BEA / Census, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026

items.headline: 10-year real yield 2.66% and breakeven 2.22% on Nov. 9; nominal 10-year 4.88%
items.take: FRED shows the 10-year Treasury inflation-indexed yield at 2.66% and the 10-year breakeven inflation rate at 2.22% on Nov. 9, with the nominal 10-year at 4.88%. Since Nov. 2 the real yield is up 4 basis points (from 2.62%) while the breakeven is down 7 basis points (from 2.29%). The nominal 10-year yield decomposes into those two pieces, so the real component now makes up most of it.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DFII10, T10YIE, DGS10)

items.headline: Henry Hub natural gas spot $2.63 per MMBtu on Nov. 3, from $2.76 on Oct. 27
items.take: FRED's daily Henry Hub series shows the spot price at $2.63 per million Btu on Nov. 3, up from $2.54 on Nov. 2 and $2.42 on Oct. 30, but below the $2.76 recorded on Oct. 27. The latest observation in the series is Nov. 3. Henry Hub is the U.S. benchmark for natural gas, so these readings are the closest official daily read on gas prices ahead of the winter heating season.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DHHNGSP)

items.headline: Capital One to present at KBW Fintech Conference Nov. 11, 11:40 a.m. ET
items.take: Capital One said in an 8-K filed Nov. 10 that it will present at the KBW Fintech Ecosystem Conference in New York on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, at 11:40 a.m. ET, with a live audio webcast on its Investor Center and a replay archived through at least Nov. 25. The filing is a Regulation FD notice and contains no financial results. Investors should treat it as a scheduling notice, not new information on the company's results.

items.headline: T. Rowe Price amends 2020 incentive plan to allow vesting after some terminations
items.take: In an 8-K filed Nov. 10, T. Rowe Price said its Executive Compensation and Management Development Committee amended the 2020 Long-Term Incentive Plan on Nov. 4, allowing continued vesting of awards for employees after certain involuntary terminations. The notice of grant was also amended to include new vesting provisions for award grants. The filing attaches the amended plan and forms of notice as exhibits and discloses no financial results.

items.headline: Overnight reverse repo usage $0.152B on Nov. 10, from $0.252B on Nov. 9
items.take: FRED's New York Fed series shows overnight reverse repurchase agreement take-up at $0.152 billion on Nov. 10, down from $0.252 billion on Nov. 9 and $0.427 billion on Nov. 3. The daily readings in the series for Nov. 3 through Nov. 10 all sit below $0.5 billion. The facility is a floor-setting tool for short-term rates, so small balances mean little cash is parked there at the Fed's offered rate.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (RRPONTSYD)

items.headline: Costco declares $30 special dividend (~$13.3B) and reauthorizes $4B buyback
items.take: Costco's board declared a special cash dividend of $30 per share, payable Dec. 4 to holders of record Nov. 24, with a total payment of approximately $13.3 billion. It also reauthorized a repurchase program of up to $4 billion, expiring in November 2030, replacing a $4 billion program adopted in 2023 under which $3.1 billion had been purchased. The special payout is far larger than the new buyback authorization, which is the clearest read on how the company is choosing to return cash.

items.headline: Bowman: backed October hold at 3-3/4 to 4%; sees 12-month core PCE at 3.3%
items.take: Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman said Nov. 10 that she supported holding the federal funds rate target range at 3-3/4 to 4 percent at last month's FOMC meeting. She said the unemployment rate has edged down to 4.1 percent in October, job gains have averaged about 80,000 per month through October, and that today's CPI suggests 12-month core PCE inflation likely moved up to 3.3 percent in October. She said progress on lowering inflation has stalled over the past two years or so, which keeps inflation, not jobs, at the center of the Fed debate.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board (Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman speech)

items.headline: Invesco October AUM $2,453.5B, down 3.3%; money market outflows $32.9B
items.take: Invesco reported preliminary month-end assets under management of $2,453.5 billion at Oct. 31, a 3.3% decrease from $2,537.8 billion at Sept. 30. Net long-term outflows were $1.0 billion, money market net outflows were $32.9 billion, market returns reduced AUM by $51 billion and FX added $0.6 billion. Those items account for the full $84.3 billion decline, so market moves and cash-fund outflows, not long-term client flows, drove the drop.

items.headline: Northern Trust issues $2B of senior notes: 5.300% due 2031, 5.700% due 2036
items.take: Northern Trust said in an 8-K that on Nov. 10 it issued $1.0 billion of 5.300% Senior Notes due 2031 and $1.0 billion of 5.700% Senior Notes due 2036 under an underwriting agreement dated Nov. 5. Interest is payable semi-annually on May 10 and Nov. 10 starting May 10, 2027. A $2.0 billion senior unsecured raise at these coupons is a data point on where a large custody bank can fund at five and ten years.

items.headline: 2-year Treasury yield 4.56% on Nov. 9, up from 4.51% on Nov. 6; 10s-2s spread 0.32
items.take: FRED data show the 2-year constant-maturity Treasury yield at 4.56% on Nov. 9, up 5 basis points from 4.51% on Nov. 6. The 10-year minus 2-year spread narrowed to 0.32 percentage point from 0.35 over the same two observations. A rising 2-year alongside a narrower spread shows shorter-dated yields moving up faster.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (DGS2, T10Y2Y)

items.headline: Waller: voted to hold because markets already price in hikes; timing 'doesn't matter'
items.take: Fed Governor Waller said Nov. 10 he supported the FOMC majority in holding policy at the most recent meeting because the Committee's communication about likely tightening had already led markets to price in some tightening. He said it is not necessary to raise rates at consecutive meetings, but that the promised hikes must be carried out in a reasonable period or market expectations and rates will fall. The message is that the debate is about follow-through on hikes, not the exact meeting.

items.headline: Waller: 6- and 12-month payroll gains near 80,000 a month, labor supply and demand 'in rough balance'
items.take: Governor Waller said October payrolls rose 165,000 with 85,000 added to estimates of the previous two months, and the unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1%. He said the 6-month and 12-month average payroll gains have been closer to 80,000 a month, a bit above most estimates of the breakeven level needed to keep unemployment steady. Averaging through the month-to-month swings gives a much slower trend than the October headline.

items.headline: Bank of England and Chancellor exchange letters on Asset Purchase Facility
items.take: The Bank of England published on Nov. 10 an exchange of letters between the Governor and the Chancellor on the Asset Purchase Facility for November 2026. The Bank's news list on the same page shows its Nov. 5 Monetary Policy Committee item titled "Bank rate increased to 4%." The page text available here carries the titles of the two letters rather than their contents, so the facility's terms are in the letters themselves.

items.headline: 30-year Treasury yield 5.26% on Nov. 6, down from 5.31% on Oct. 30
items.take: FRED's constant-maturity series shows the 30-year Treasury yield at 5.26% on Nov. 6, down 5 basis points from 5.31% on Oct. 30. With the 10-year at 4.86% the same day, the 30-year sat 40 basis points above it. The long end moved in the same direction as the front of the curve over the week.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Fed Board approves Mutual Federal Bancorp holding-company applications in Chicago
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board announced on Nov. 9 its approval of two applications by Mutual Federal Bancorp, MHC, and MFB Bancorp, Inc., both of Chicago, Illinois. The approvals allow a new top-tier holding company, MFB Bancorp, Inc., which would become a savings and loan holding company by acquiring Mutual Federal Bank of Chicago. The approval concerns a holding-company structure, not monetary policy.

items.headline: Steel Dynamics adds $3.0B buyback authorization, declares $0.53 dividend
items.take: Steel Dynamics said Nov. 9 its board authorized an additional $3.0 billion share repurchase program, effective immediately and additive to the prior $1.5 billion program, which had $216 million remaining on Sept. 30, 2026. The board also declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.53 per share, payable on or about Jan. 8, 2027 to holders of record Dec. 31, 2026. The new authorization is more than 13 times what was left on the old one, a sizable step up in planned capital return.

items.headline: Rakuten and AST SpaceMobile form Japan satellite JV tied to ~$1B in government support
items.take: Rakuten Group and AST SpaceMobile agreed to establish Rakuten AST, Inc. on Nov. 6 (Japan time) to build a direct-to-device LEO satellite network in Japan, with Rakuten holding 51% of voting rights and AST SpaceMobile's Japanese subsidiary 49%. The release says the venture is expected to receive up to 148 billion yen (approximately $1 billion) in support over about three years from Japan's J-LEO project, with domestic operations targeted by the end of March 2029. The venture pairs a Japanese-government-backed funding award with AST SpaceMobile's satellite supply role.

items.headline: ECB's Cipollone: digital euro pilot to start in 2H 2027, needs law adopted by year-end
items.take: In remarks to the European Parliament's economics committee on Nov. 10, ECB Executive Board member Piero Cipollone said the digital euro pilot starts in the second half of 2027 with 36 selected payment service providers, and that first issuance can be set only after the Regulation is adopted. He said a swift end to trilogue talks would allow adoption of the Single Currency Package by the end of the year, and noted that on Nov. 2 the Pontes platform settled the European Stability Mechanism's first digitally native benchmark bond of EUR 1 billion. The timeline now hinges on legislation rather than technical readiness, by his account.

items.headline: SOFR 3.88% on Nov. 9, down from 3.95% a week earlier; Fed assets $6.748T
items.take: FRED shows the secured overnight financing rate at 3.88% on Nov. 9, down 7 basis points from 3.95% on Nov. 2, while overnight reverse repurchase take-up was $0.152 billion on Nov. 10. Federal Reserve total assets were $6,748,145 million (about $6.748 trillion) in the week of Nov. 4, up $2.5 billion from $6,745,635 million on Oct. 28. Repo funding rates drifting lower with almost no reverse repo usage points to ample cash in overnight markets.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: EUR/USD at 1.1154 and USD/JPY at 158.23 on Nov. 6
items.take: FRED daily exchange rates show the euro at $1.1154 on Nov. 6, down from $1.1235 on Nov. 5 and $1.1163 on Oct. 30. The yen rate was 158.23 per dollar on Nov. 6 versus 157.47 on Oct. 30, a move of 0.76 yen per dollar over the week. The euro's one-day drop was the largest of the six observations in the series pulled, while the yen has stayed in a narrow 157-158.5 range.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Global refinery inputs fell 4.8M b/d in 2Q26, then rose 1.8M b/d in 3Q: EIA
items.take: EIA, citing Kpler data, said global crude refinery inputs fell by 4.8 million b/d, or 6%, in the second quarter of 2026 after the start of conflict in the Middle East in late February, then increased by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter. China's inputs fell 2.1 million b/d in 2Q26 and a further 0.8 million b/d in 3Q26, while Kuwait, the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Iran together saw inputs rise 0.4 million b/d in 3Q26 after second-quarter declines. The third-quarter rebound recovered well under half of the second-quarter drop.

items.headline: October CPI rises 0.4% after 0.6% in September; core up 0.3%
items.take: BLS reported the CPI-U increased 0.4% seasonally adjusted in October after rising 0.6% in September, and the index for all items less food and energy rose 0.3%, as it did in September and August. The not seasonally adjusted index rose 0.2% to 337.511. Core running at 0.3% for a third straight month is the pace to watch against the energy-driven headline swings.

items.headline: CPI: energy up 0.7% in October after 5.2% in September; food up 0.5%
items.take: The BLS energy index rose 0.7% in October following a 5.2% increase in September, with gasoline up 1.0% seasonally adjusted (down 0.7% before seasonal adjustment) and electricity up 0.9%. Food rose 0.5%, with food at home up 0.4% and food away from home up 0.5%. Energy's contribution cooled sharply from September, but grocery and restaurant prices both firmed.

items.headline: CPI shelter rises 0.3% in October; used cars fall 1.2%, motor vehicle insurance up 0.7%
items.take: The BLS shelter index rose 0.3% in October after 0.4% in September, with owners' equivalent rent up 0.3% and rent up 0.2%, and shelter accounted for over thirty percent of the monthly all-items increase. Used cars and trucks fell 1.2% after rising 0.7%, while motor vehicle insurance rose 0.7% and recreation rose 0.8%. Offsetting moves in vehicles and services kept core at 0.3%.

items.headline: BLS cannot publish most 12-month CPI changes for October; gasoline up 37.4% on year
items.take: BLS said it did not collect October 2025 survey data because of a lapse in appropriations, so it cannot publish October 2026 12-month changes for indexes lacking October 2025 values; the headline all-items 12-month rate is shown as unavailable. Where published, gasoline was up 37.4% over 12 months and used cars and trucks down 3.3%. That leaves monthly changes as the main inflation read from this release.

items.headline: Real average hourly earnings unchanged in October as pay and CPI both rise 0.4%
items.take: BLS reported real average hourly earnings for all employees were unchanged from September to October (seasonally adjusted), as a 0.4% rise in average hourly earnings matched a 0.4% rise in the CPI-U. For production and nonsupervisory employees, real hourly earnings rose 0.1% and real weekly earnings fell 0.3% on a 0.3% shorter average workweek. Over-the-year comparisons are unavailable because of the missing October 2025 CPI data.

items.headline: High-yield spread 3.34 points on Nov. 9, down from 3.43 on Nov. 2; investment grade 0.91
items.take: FRED data show the ICE BofA US High Yield option-adjusted spread at 3.34 percentage points on Nov. 9, versus 3.43 on Nov. 2 and 3.48 on Nov. 5. The investment-grade corporate spread was 0.91 on Nov. 9, down from 0.94 on Nov. 2. Both spreads sit near the low end of the past week's range.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Initial jobless claims 189,000 in week ended Oct. 31, lowest of six weekly readings
items.take: FRED data show seasonally adjusted initial jobless claims at 189,000 for the week ended Oct. 31, down from 195,000 in each of the prior two weeks and 200,000 for the week ended Oct. 10. It is the lowest of the six weekly observations since Sept. 26. Low claims alongside October's 165,000 payroll gain point to a labor market with few layoffs.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Waller: further tightening needed "sooner rather than later" to bring inflation to 2%
items.take: In a Nov. 10 speech in London, Governor Christopher Waller said he voted with the FOMC majority to hold the policy rate at the most recent meeting, but that inflation remains too high and further tightening will be needed "sooner rather than later." He said Q3 real GDP rose 3.4 percent in the initial estimate, the unemployment rate was 4.1 percent in October, and 6- and 12-month average payroll gains are closer to 80,000 a month. The speech makes clear that at least one voting-level official sees the timing of the next hike as flexible but the direction as set.

items.headline: Waller on labor market: "low hire, low fire" for over a year, with 5M+ monthly separations and hires
items.take: Governor Waller said that although September net job creation was 60,000, more than 5 million people left their jobs and more than 5 million were hired that month. He described the labor market as "low hire, low fire" for over a year and asked whether stability means a healthy market, noting the share of adults 25 and older with at least a bachelor's degree rose from 28 percent to 37 percent since 2010. Low gross flows matter because they can weigh on productivity and real wage growth even when the unemployment rate is steady.

items.headline: ECB's Lane: LLM-based tone measures track hawkish and dovish phases of ECB communication
items.take: In a Nov. 10 keynote at the Bank of England Watchers Conference in London, ECB Executive Board member Philip Lane said new ECB staff LLM-based measures of the tone of monetary policy communication become more hawkish during tightening phases and more dovish during easing periods, closely tracking the deposit facility rate. He added that information in ECB policy statements can improve forecasts of euro-area core inflation several quarters ahead. The speech is about communication method rather than a new policy signal.

items.headline: U.S. crude imports from Venezuela hit 701,000 b/d in July, most since May 2017: EIA
items.take: EIA's Nov. 6 analysis says U.S. crude oil imports from Venezuela averaged 701,000 barrels per day in July 2026, the most since May 2017, before easing to 655,000 b/d in August. Imports started the year at 200,000 b/d. EIA attributes the rise to high U.S. refinery crude demand because of high global refinery margins and eased U.S. restrictions on purchases from Venezuela. The shift matters for Gulf Coast refiners configured for heavy sour grades.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration (Today in Energy)

items.headline: Refiners cut gasoline yield below 45% in 2026 to favor diesel and jet fuel: EIA
items.take: EIA's Nov. 5 analysis of Petroleum Supply Monthly data through August says U.S. refinery gasoline yields averaged less than 45% from January through August 2026 and were below the five-year (2021-2025) low in every month, while distillate yields were above the five-year average in every month. The U.S. refinery fleet exceeded a 12% average jet fuel yield for the first time in March and has stayed at or above it through August. EIA ties the shift to higher margins on middle distillates amid constrained global supply.
items.source_name: U.S. Energy Information Administration (Today in Energy)

items.headline: 10-year Treasury yield 4.86% on Nov. 6, down from 4.94% on Oct. 30; 2-year at 4.51%
items.take: FRED data show the 10-year constant-maturity Treasury yield at 4.86% on Nov. 6, down 8 basis points from 4.94% on Oct. 30, and the 2-year at 4.51%, down 5 basis points from 4.56%. The 10-year minus 2-year spread was 0.32 percentage point on Nov. 9, and the 10-year breakeven inflation rate was 2.22% that day. A 10-year real yield of 2.63% on Nov. 6 shows most of the nominal yield is real rather than inflation compensation.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.headline: Brent spot $107.03 and WTI $99.64 on Nov. 3, below $123.10 and $103.37 on Oct. 27
items.take: FRED's latest daily spot series show Brent at $107.03 per barrel on Nov. 3, down $16.07 from $123.10 on Oct. 27, and WTI at $99.64, down $3.73 from $103.37. The Brent-WTI gap was $7.39 on Nov. 3. Henry Hub natural gas spot was $2.63 per million Btu on Nov. 3. Brent's larger decline narrowed the gap between the two benchmarks over the week.
items.source_name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (EIA spot prices)

items.headline: KKR Q3: total revenues $4.56B, GAAP EPS $1.19, AUM $804B
items.take: KKR's Nov. 9 release reports third-quarter 2026 total revenues of $4,563.7 million versus $5,526.0 million a year earlier, and net income attributable to KKR & Co. Inc. of $1.19 per common share versus $0.90. Adjusted Net Income was $1.6 billion ($1.78 per adjusted share), up 29% year over year, and AUM was $804 billion, up 11%. GAAP revenue and earnings per share moved in opposite directions, so the revenue line alone does not capture the quarter.
items.source_name: KKR & Co. Inc. Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC EDGAR EX-99.1)

items.headline: AST SpaceMobile Q3 revenue $42.3M vs $14.7M; net loss $0.44 per share
items.take: AST SpaceMobile's Nov. 9 release reports third-quarter 2026 revenues of $42.3 million versus $14.7 million in the third quarter of 2025, and basic and diluted net loss per Class A share of $(0.44) versus $(0.45). The release says BlueBirds 11, 12 and 13 unfolded successfully and are in operation in orbit, and targets approximately 45 BlueBird satellites in orbit by middle 2027. Revenue nearly tripled from a small base while the per-share loss was little changed.
items.source_name: AST SpaceMobile Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC EDGAR EX-99.1)

items.headline: QXO prelim Q3: net sales about $4.90B, GAAP net loss about $123M
items.take: QXO's preliminary, unaudited release puts third-quarter 2026 net sales at approximately $4.90 billion versus $2.73 billion a year earlier, with a GAAP net loss of approximately $123 million versus $139 million and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $557 million versus $301 million. The 2026 figures include Kodiak Building Partners from April 1 and TopBuild from July 1, neither of which was in the prior-year quarter. Acquisitions, not organic trends alone, drive the year-over-year jump; full results are due Nov. 12.
items.source_name: QXO, Inc.: Q3 2026 Preliminary Financial Information (SEC EDGAR EX-99.1)

items.headline: CNH files 8-K with Q3 2026 results release and investor presentation
items.take: CNH Industrial's 8-K reports under Item 2.02 a Nov. 9, 2026 press release on third-quarter results, furnished as Exhibit 99.1, and under Item 7.01 a results slide presentation for a Nov. 9 investor call, furnished as Exhibit 99.2. The filing's cover page carries no financial figures, which sit in the exhibits. AlphaGen will report the numbers once read from the release itself.
items.source_name: SEC EDGAR: CNH Industrial N.V. Form 8-K, Nov. 9, 2026

items.headline: Qualys files 8-K on Q3 2026 results; conference call held same day
items.take: Qualys's 8-K, signed Nov. 9, 2026 by its CFO, furnishes under Item 2.02 a press release announcing results for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, and says the company would hold a conference call that day. Results figures are in Exhibit 99.1, not the cover filing. The information is furnished rather than filed for Exchange Act Section 18 purposes.
items.source_name: SEC EDGAR: Qualys, Inc. Form 8-K, Nov. 9, 2026

items.headline: Kemper files 8-K on third-quarter 2026 results; supplement and call deck posted
items.take: Kemper's 8-K, signed Nov. 9, 2026, reports under Item 2.02 a press release on third-quarter 2026 financial results and lists a Q3 investor supplement (Exhibit 99.2) and an earnings call presentation (Exhibit 99.3) alongside it. The cover filing contains no figures. Kemper had already published a preliminary Q3 item on the Wire on Oct. 29, so the full release is the next data point to compare.

items.headline: October payrolls rise 165,000; unemployment rate 4.1%
items.take: BLS reported total nonfarm payroll employment rose by 165,000 in October and the unemployment rate changed little at 4.1%, with 7.1 million people unemployed. The rate has stayed in a range of 4.1% to 4.3% since March. The October gain is well above the 12-month average monthly gain of 48,000 that BLS cites, which frames the month as a pickup rather than a trend.

items.headline: BLS revises August, September payrolls up by a combined 84,000
items.take: BLS revised August payroll growth up 53,000 to +186,000 and September up 31,000 to +60,000. Together the two months are 84,000 higher than previously reported (53,000 + 31,000). The upward revisions mean September's initial +29,000 reading understated hiring by more than half of the revised figure.

items.headline: Average hourly earnings up 0.4% in October to $38.00; 3.1% over 12 months
items.take: BLS said average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls rose 14 cents, or 0.4%, to $38.00 in October, and are up 3.1% over the past 12 months. For production and nonsupervisory employees, earnings rose 12 cents, or 0.4%, to $32.75. Wage growth at this pace is a data point the Fed will read alongside inflation figures due next week.

items.headline: Participation 61.9%, employment-population ratio 59.3% in October
items.take: BLS reported the labor force participation rate at 61.9% and the employment-population ratio at 59.3% in October, both little changed. Long-term unemployed workers numbered 2.0 million, or 27.6% of the unemployed, and those working part time for economic reasons rose by 339,000 to 4.8 million. The rise in involuntary part-time work is the softer detail beneath the headline payroll gain.

items.headline: Arista Q3 revenue $3,657.6M vs $2,308.3M; GAAP diluted EPS $1.22 vs $0.67
items.take: Arista reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $3,657.6 million versus $2,308.3 million a year earlier, a 58.5% increase, with GAAP diluted EPS of $1.22 versus $0.67. The company guided fourth-quarter revenue of $3.9-$4.0 billion. Guidance now sits above this quarter's level, so the Q4 print becomes the next check on that trajectory.
items.source_name: Arista Networks Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

items.headline: Uber Q3 revenue $14,766M, up 10%; GAAP diluted EPS $0.25 vs $3.11
items.take: Uber reported Q3 2026 revenue of $14,766 million versus $13,467 million a year earlier and GAAP diluted EPS of $0.25 versus $3.11; the release says Q3 2025 net income included a $4.9 billion tax valuation release benefit and a $1.5 billion pre-tax benefit from equity investment revaluations. Q4 Gross Bookings guidance is $63.25-$65.25 billion, growth of 18% to 22% on a constant-currency basis. The prior-year tax and investment items make the EPS comparison a poor read on underlying change.

items.headline: Prudential Q3 net income $1.388B, $3.96 per share; returns $741M to holders
items.take: Prudential Financial reported third-quarter net income attributable to the company of $1.388 billion, or $3.96 per Common share, versus $4.01 a year earlier. Capital returned to shareholders totaled $741 million, including $250 million of share repurchases and $491 million of dividends, versus $731 million in the year-ago quarter. Per-share earnings were slightly lower while capital returned was slightly higher.
items.source_name: Prudential Financial Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

items.headline: Marvell agrees to acquire Lumentum in all-stock deal at 4.500 shares per share
items.take: Marvell Technology entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Lumentum Holdings on Nov. 1, under which each Lumentum common share will be converted into the right to receive 4.500 shares of Marvell common stock. Closing is pending, subject to Lumentum and Marvell stockholder approvals, HSR expiration and an effective Form S-4. The outside date in the agreement is Nov. 1, 2027, so the regulatory and shareholder path will run well past this year.

items.headline: JOLTS: September job openings little changed at 7.5M; hires 5.4M
items.take: BLS reported job openings little changed at 7.5 million (rate 4.5%) in September, with hires little changed at 5.4 million (3.4%) and total separations at 5.3 million (3.3%, unchanged). August openings were revised up by 111,000 to 7.2 million. Openings and hires moving little suggests the labor market data in this report showed no sharp shift in the month.
items.source_name: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Summary, September 2026

items.headline: JOLTS: quits rise to 3.4M in September; layoffs little changed at 1.6M
items.take: BLS said quits increased to 3.4 million in September (rate 2.1%), up 375,000 from a year earlier, while layoffs and discharges were little changed at 1.6 million (1.0%). August quits were revised down by 22,000 to 3.0 million and August layoffs revised up by 127,000 to 1.8 million. A higher quits count alongside steady layoffs is the pairing watchers of labor-market turnover track.
items.source_name: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Summary, September 2026

items.headline: Knife River Q3 revenue $1,275.6M, up 6%; updates 2026 guidance
items.take: Knife River reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1,275.6 million versus $1,203.7 million a year earlier, net income of $137.9 million versus $143.2 million, and diluted EPS of $2.43 versus $2.52. Adjusted EBITDA was $271.7 million versus $272.8 million. The company updated full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $3,375-$3,425 million and adjusted EBITDA of $475-$505 million, citing near-term headwinds.
items.source_name: Knife River Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99)

items.headline: Ball Q3 net sales $4.19B vs $3.38B; comparable EPS $1.10 vs $1.03
items.take: Ball reported Q3 2026 net sales of $4,188 million versus $3,379 million, a net loss attributable to Ball of $94 million (diluted loss per share of $0.36) versus earnings of $321 million ($1.18). Comparable diluted EPS was $1.10 versus $1.03. For 2026 it expects comparable diluted EPS growth of 10-plus percent and free cash flow in the range of $900 million.

items.headline: Xometry Q3 revenue $252M, up 40%; raises full-year revenue growth outlook
items.take: Xometry reported Q3 2026 revenue of $252.4 million versus $180.7 million a year earlier, with diluted EPS of $0.03 versus a loss of $0.23. It now expects 2026 revenue growth of at least 37%, up from a prior 33-34%, and Q4 revenue of $254-$256 million. The raised outlook comes with a return to GAAP profit for the quarter.

items.headline: HNI Q3 net sales $1.59B, up 133%; GAAP diluted EPS $1.23 vs $0.88
items.take: HNI reported Q3 2026 net sales of $1,592.9 million versus $683.8 million a year earlier, with organic net sales up 5.6%. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.23 versus $0.88 and net income was $90.0 million versus $41.2 million. The company expects 2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS growth of 20-25%.

items.headline: LGI Homes Q3 revenue $444.5M, up 10.2%; narrows 2026 closings to 4,600-4,800
items.take: LGI Homes reported Q3 2026 total revenues of $444.5 million versus $403.5 million a year earlier and diluted EPS of $1.05 versus $0.85. Net income was $24.6 million. The builder narrowed its full-year home closings outlook to between 4,600 and 4,800 and maintained the rest of its 2026 guidance.

items.headline: Patria Q3 fee-related earnings $52.8M, up 7%; declares $0.1625 dividend
items.take: Patria reported Q3 2026 fee-related earnings of $52.8 million versus $49.5 million in Q3 2025, a 53.7% FRE margin, and distributable earnings of $46.9 million, or $0.30 per share. It raised $2.4 billion in the quarter and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.1625 per share payable December 11, 2026.

items.headline: Amneal Q3 revenue $863M, up 10%; raises 2026 revenue and EBITDA guidance
items.take: Amneal reported Q3 2026 net revenue of $863 million versus $785 million a year earlier, a GAAP diluted loss of $0.06 per share versus earnings of $0.01, and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.26 versus $0.17. It updated 2026 guidance to net revenue of $3.15 billion to $3.25 billion (prior $3.10 billion to $3.20 billion) and adjusted EBITDA of $800 million to $815 million (prior $750 million to $780 million). The raised ranges sit alongside lower operating cash flow guidance of $325 million to $375 million, from $350 million to $400 million.

items.headline: Luckin Coffee Q3 net revenues RMB17.9B, up 17.0%; same-store sales negative 11.1%
items.take: Luckin Coffee reported Q3 2026 total net revenues of RMB17,891.5 million (US$2,666.0 million) versus RMB15,287.1 million a year earlier, and net income of RMB1,858.9 million versus RMB1,278.3 million. Self-operated same-store sales growth was negative 11.1%, against 14.3% in Q3 2025, and the company ended the quarter with 38,909 stores. Revenue growth is coming from store count and customers rather than from existing-store sales.

items.headline: Luckin Coffee board approves new share repurchase program of up to US$500M
items.take: Luckin Coffee's board approved a new share repurchase program of up to US$500 million, running for 12 months and starting after the existing US$500 million authorization is fully used or expires. As of Sept. 30, 2026, the existing program had repurchased US$391.0 million of shares. That leaves roughly US$109 million of the current authorization unused at quarter-end.

items.headline: IPC Q3 revenue $212M; net result $60M includes $45M gain on Canada asset sale
items.take: International Petroleum Corporation reported Q3 2026 revenue of USD 211.955 million versus USD 172.297 million a year earlier and a net result of USD 59.901 million versus USD 3.802 million, including a gain on the sale of assets in Canada of MUSD 45. It raised 2026 operating cash flow guidance to MUSD 275-350 from MUSD 230-330, assuming Brent of USD 80 to 110 per barrel for the rest of 2026, and kept production guidance at 44,000 to 47,000 boepd. The guidance revision rests on a higher oil price assumption, so it moves with the commodity.

items.headline: IPG Photonics Q3 revenue $287.5M, up 15%; GAAP EPS $0.47 vs $0.18
items.take: IPG Photonics reported Q3 2026 revenue of $287.5 million versus $250.8 million a year earlier, GAAP diluted EPS of $0.47 versus $0.18, and adjusted EPS of $0.61 versus $0.35. It guided Q4 revenue to $265 million to $295 million and adjusted EPS to $0.30 to $0.60, assuming no contribution from the Lumibird Medical acquisition. A fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth is the context for a Q4 range that brackets the Q3 revenue level.

items.headline: ADT Q3 revenue $1,349M, up 4%; guidance withdrawn amid Thrive deal
items.take: ADT reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1,349 million versus $1,298 million, income from continuing operations of $0.20 per diluted share versus $0.17, and adjusted EPS of $0.24 versus $0.23. The company said it is not providing financial guidance and is withdrawing previously issued guidance; on Oct. 29 it agreed to be acquired by Thrive Holdings for $10.00 per share in cash, with closing expected in Q1 2027 subject to stockholder and U.S. antitrust approval. With a fixed cash price on the table, the quarterly numbers matter mainly for deal-closing conditions.

items.headline: BioNTech Q3 revenue EUR 1,289.2M vs EUR 1,518.9M; FY revenue range EUR 1.7-1.9B
items.take: BioNTech reported Q3 2026 revenue of €1,289.2 million versus €1,518.9 million and IFRS diluted EPS of €0.73 versus €(0.12). Its full-year 2026 revenue guidance is now €1,700 million to €1,900 million, versus €1,600 million to €1,900 million previously. Cash, cash equivalents and security investments were €16,163.8 million at Sept. 30, which keeps the focus on how that balance is deployed.

items.headline: Apollo reports Q3; declares $0.5625 dividend; AUM about $1.07T, origination $114B
items.take: Apollo said it had approximately $1.07 trillion of assets under management at Sept. 30, 2026, with origination reaching a new high of $114 billion in the quarter. It declared a cash dividend of $0.5625 per share, payable Nov. 30 to holders of record at the close of business Nov. 18. Origination volume is the input the firm itself points to as the driver of its model.

items.headline: Fiserv Q3 GAAP revenue $5.20B, down 1%; organic flat; outlook affirmed
items.take: Fiserv reported Q3 2026 GAAP revenue of $5.20 billion, a 1% decline from a year earlier, with organic revenue flat: Merchant Solutions down 2% and Financial Solutions up 2%. Adjusted EPS was $1.75, and the company affirmed 2026 organic revenue of (1%) to 0% and adjusted EPS of $7.20 to $7.40. Flat organic growth with a guidance affirmation puts the focus on whether Financial Solutions' return to growth can offset Merchant weakness.

items.headline: Fiserv books $6.45B goodwill impairment, raises Project Elevate savings goal to $1B
items.take: Fiserv's Q3 2026 GAAP diluted EPS was $(11.17), versus $1.46 a year earlier, reflecting a non-cash goodwill impairment of $6.45 billion. The company raised its Project Elevate savings target to $1 billion from $500 million and said it expects to repurchase $500 million of shares in Q4 2026. A non-cash charge of this size explains the gap between GAAP and adjusted results, so adjusted EPS of $1.75 is the better read on operating trend.

items.headline: Sportradar Q3 revenue rises 24% to EUR 363M; FY2026 outlook reiterated
items.take: Sportradar reported Q3 2026 revenue of EUR 362.5 million versus EUR 292.1 million, up 24%, with profit of EUR 27 million and Adjusted EBITDA of EUR 102 million (28.2% margin). It reiterated 2026 guidance of 19% to 21% constant-currency revenue growth and 24% to 27% Adjusted EBITDA growth. The release also cites an agreement to divest Atrium Sports for US$170 million, excluded from guidance.

items.headline: Merck KGaA to divest CDMO business to Lonza for a mid-triple-digit million euro sum
items.take: Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany signed a definitive agreement to divest its CDMO business within Life Science to Lonza for what the release calls a mid-triple-digit million-euro amount. The deal covers sites in Carlsbad, Madison, Verona, St. Louis and Indianapolis, excludes BioReliance Contract Testing Services, and is expected to close in mid-2027 subject to customary regulatory approvals. Merck KGaA frames it as sharpening focus on innovation-driven businesses.

items.headline: RBA Monetary Policy Board decision due Nov. 3 at 2:30 p.m. AEDT, 10:30 p.m. ET
items.take: The Reserve Bank of Australia's calendar lists a Monetary Policy Board meeting on Nov. 2-3, with the decision statement and the Statement on Monetary Policy both scheduled for Nov. 3 at 2:30 p.m. AEDT and a media conference at 3:30 p.m. AEDT. The Chart Pack follows Nov. 4 at 11:30 a.m. AEDT, and Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser speaks Nov. 5. The decision lands in the Asia session ahead of U.S. trading Tuesday.

items.headline: Treasury lists quarterly refunding documents for Nov. 4 release
items.take: Treasury's quarterly refunding page says the next release of the refunding policy statement, TBAC report and minutes, recommended financing table, auction schedule and buyback schedule is scheduled for Nov. 4, 2026. The page lists the preceding release on Aug. 5 and a financing-estimates release scheduled for Nov. 2. Refunding statements set the tone for coupon auction sizes, making Nov. 4 the key Treasury supply date this week.

items.headline: Entergy furnishes third-quarter 2026 earnings release in Nov. 2 8-K
items.take: Entergy Corporation filed a Form 8-K under Items 2.02 and 7.01 reporting that it issued a press release on Nov. 2, 2026 announcing results of operations and financial condition for the third quarter of 2026, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing is a combined report with Entergy's utility subsidiaries. The 8-K itself carries no figures, which sit in the exhibit.

items.headline: Publix files Nov. 2 8-K with third-quarter 2026 results
items.take: Publix Super Markets filed a Form 8-K under Item 2.02 stating that on Nov. 2, 2026 it issued a press release reporting its third-quarter results for 2026, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The 8-K body contains no sales or earnings figures. Publix is employee-owned and not exchange-listed, so its filings are the main public read on grocery-sector results.

items.headline: BWX Technologies files Q3 2026 earnings 8-K for quarter ended Sept. 30
items.take: BWX Technologies filed a Form 8-K under Item 2.02 stating that on Nov. 2, 2026 it issued a press release announcing financial results for the third quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The 8-K body itself contains no revenue or earnings figures. Investors will look to the exhibit for backlog and guidance detail.

items.headline: onsemi to acquire Ferric for $600M cash plus up to $175M in milestones
items.take: onsemi announced an agreement to acquire Ferric, Inc., an integrated voltage regulator technology company, for $600 million in cash at closing plus up to $175 million in additional cash tied to revenue milestones, funded with cash on hand. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. onsemi also raised its 2030 AI data center revenue target by $500 million to greater than $3 billion, which frames the deal as a bet on power delivery for AI processors.

items.headline: Kewaunee Scientific agrees to acquire Nycom for $55M initial base price
items.take: Kewaunee Scientific entered a definitive agreement to acquire Nycom, Inc. for an initial base purchase price of $55 million, subject to adjustments based on Nycom's Adjusted EBITDA and customary post-closing items. $20 million is payable via a subordinated promissory note and $5 million in newly issued Kewaunee shares, with the remaining cash portion funded by cash on hand and PNC Bank financing. Closing is expected in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, subject to customary conditions, so the price is a starting figure rather than a final one.

items.headline: NorthStrive SPAC agrees business combination with Nuclea Energy at $350M enterprise value
items.take: NorthStrive Acquisition Corp I announced a definitive Business Combination Agreement with Nuclea Energy, a company developing advanced nuclear technologies, at an enterprise value for Nuclea of $350 million, subject to adjustments at closing. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to shareholder approvals, an effective Form S-4, Nasdaq listing approval and other conditions including completion of Nuclea's pending Moltex acquisition. The combined company is expected to be renamed Nuclea-X Inc.; the SPAC completed a $100 million IPO on Aug. 19, 2026, so the deal is a pending, condition-heavy path to a listing.
items.source_name: NorthStrive Acquisition Corp I, press release (GlobeNewswire)

items.headline: Alexander's Q3 net income $27.4M vs $6.0M; FFO $7.07 per diluted share vs $2.91
items.take: Alexander's reported net income of $27.4 million, or $5.33 per diluted share, for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, versus $6.0 million, or $1.16 per diluted share, a year earlier. FFO (non-GAAP) was $36.3 million, or $7.07 per diluted share, versus $14.9 million, or $2.91. Revenues were $72.1 million versus $53.4 million; the release separately states nine-month net income included $148.0 million of income from the net gain on sale of the Rego Park I property.

items.headline: Lightbridge Q3 net loss $8.3M vs $4.1M; cash $236.7M at Sept. 30
items.take: Lightbridge reported a net loss of $8.3 million, or $0.23 per basic and diluted share, for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, versus $4.1 million, or $0.16, a year earlier, with no revenue in either period. Cash and cash equivalents were $236.7 million at Sept. 30 versus $201.9 million at Dec. 31, 2025, an increase of $34.8 million. R&D expense was $5.3 million versus $2.0 million, which accounts for much of the wider loss.

items.headline: Krystal Biotech Q3 product revenue $127.3M vs $97.8M; diluted EPS $2.05 vs $2.66
items.take: Krystal Biotech reported net product revenue of $127.3 million for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, versus $97.8 million a year earlier. Net income was $63.1 million, or $2.05 per diluted share, versus $79.4 million, or $2.66 per diluted share, in the prior-year quarter. Revenue rose while net income and EPS fell, so the comparison turns on costs below the revenue line. The company also announced a share repurchase program of up to $400 million.

items.headline: Kosmos Energy Q3 oil and gas revenue $410.1M vs $311.0M; net loss $0.07 per share
items.take: Kosmos Energy reported Q3 2026 oil and gas revenue of $410.1 million versus $311.0 million in Q3 2025, a net loss of $43.0 million, or $(0.07) per diluted share, versus $(0.26) a year earlier. Full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance of approximately $350 million is unchanged, and gross LNG cargo liftings are expected at the upper end of the 32-36 guidance range. The loss narrowed sharply on a per-share basis from the prior-year quarter.

items.headline: Capital Power Q3 net income C$67M vs C$153M; raises sustaining capex target
items.take: Capital Power reported Q3 2026 revenues and other income of $831 million versus $1,213 million a year earlier, net income of $67 million versus $153 million, and diluted EPS of $0.37 versus $0.94 (release figures in millions of dollars). Revised 2026 guidance lists AFFO of $890 million to $1,010 million, adjusted EBITDA of $1,565 million to $1,765 million, and sustaining capital expenditures of $350 million to $370 million versus an original $290 million to $330 million. The company also increased its annual common dividend by 2%.

items.headline: Tower Semiconductor Q3 revenue $526M vs $396M; guides Q4 revenue to $600M
items.take: Tower Semiconductor reported Q3 2026 revenue of $526 million versus $396 million in Q3 2025. For Q4 2026 it guides revenue of $600 million, with an upward or downward range of 5%, which it says represents an increase of 36% year over year and 14% quarter over quarter at the midpoint. The company says the year closes at $2 billion of annual revenue.

items.headline: Riksbank calendar: policy meeting Nov. 3, decision published Nov. 4
items.take: The Riksbank's 2026 calendar lists a monetary policy meeting on Nov. 3 titled "Decision on monetary policy including the policy rate." It lists Nov. 4 for the "Publication of monetary policy decision, including the policy rate, and the Monetary Policy Update." The pages show no times or rate level, so the decision itself is the next official data point for Swedish policy.

items.headline: Fed calendar: no FOMC meeting in November; next is Dec. 8-9
items.take: The Federal Reserve's 2026 FOMC calendar lists the most recent meeting as Oct. 27-28 and the next as Dec. 8-9, which is marked as a meeting associated with a Summary of Economic Projections. The Board's November calendar lists no FOMC meeting. That leaves the Fed's scheduled data releases and speeches as the main official Fed inputs this month.

items.headline: Fed to release minutes of Oct. 27-28 FOMC meeting on Nov. 18 at 2:00 p.m.
items.take: The Federal Reserve's November calendar lists FOMC Minutes for the meeting of Oct. 27-28 on Nov. 18 at 2:00 p.m. The minutes are the Fed's written record of the committee's discussion at that meeting. They are the next official FOMC document on the calendar before the December meeting.

items.headline: Fed lists Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey for Nov. 2 at 2:00 p.m.
items.take: The Federal Reserve's November calendar lists the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey on Bank Lending Practices (SLOOS) on Nov. 2 at 2:00 p.m. The survey covers banks' lending standards and demand, so it is the official read on credit availability for the week.

items.headline: Fed week ahead: H.4.1 on Nov. 5, Bowman remarks and G.19 on Nov. 6
items.take: The Fed's calendar lists H.4.1, Factors Affecting Reserve Balances, on Nov. 5 at 4:30 p.m. On Nov. 6 it lists a discussion with Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle W. Bowman on supervision and regulation at the University of Mississippi Banking and Finance Symposium at 12:15 p.m., and G.19, Consumer Credit, at 3:00 p.m. H.15 interest-rate data is listed each business day at 4:15 p.m.

items.headline: Fed: Veterans Day holiday Nov. 11 moves daily and weekly releases to Nov. 12
items.take: The Fed's November calendar lists Veterans Day on Nov. 11 and says releases scheduled that day move to Thursday, Nov. 12. The calendar also lists the Beige Book on Nov. 25 at 2:00 p.m. and a Thanksgiving Day holiday on Nov. 26. Data users should plan for the shifted H.15 and H.4.1 dates.

items.headline: BoJ Outlook: FY2026 real GDP median +0.7%, core CPI median +2.5%
items.take: The Bank of Japan's October 2026 Outlook Report, dated Oct. 30, puts the Policy Board median forecast for FY2026 real GDP at +0.7% (July: +0.6%) and CPI less fresh food at +2.5% (July: +2.5%). For FY2027 the medians are +0.7% for real GDP (July: +0.8%) and +2.6% for CPI less fresh food (July: +2.4%). The report says the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate, so the 2027 inflation revision is the part that bears on the pace of that path.
items.source_name: Bank of Japan, Outlook for Economic Activity and Prices (Oct. 2026)

items.headline: Treasury calendar: bill auctions run Nov. 2-5, 13- and 26-week first
items.take: Treasury's tentative auction schedule lists 13-week and 26-week bills on Monday, Nov. 2 (announced Oct. 29, settling Nov. 5) and a 6-week bill on Tuesday, Nov. 3. A 17-week bill follows Wednesday, Nov. 4, and 4-week and 8-week bills Thursday, Nov. 5, all settling Nov. 10. The calendar lists no offering amounts or times, so the sizes announced Nov. 3 are the figures to watch.

items.headline: L.B. Foster's CXT closes $52.18M cash purchase of Dulworth Enterprises assets
items.take: L.B. Foster said in its 8-K that CXT Incorporated, a wholly owned subsidiary, agreed to buy Dulworth Enterprises' operating assets for $52,180,000 in cash, subject to customary indemnification holdbacks, and that the transaction closed Oct. 28, 2026. It was funded with cash on hand and available funds from its existing revolving credit facility. The assets will be integrated into the Precast Concrete Products business unit.

items.headline: Climb Global Solutions buys France's NeoVAD for about €16.0M
items.take: Climb Global Solutions said in an 8-K that on Oct. 21, 2026 it entered into a Sale and Purchase Agreement and purchased 100% of the issued and outstanding shares of NeoVAD for an aggregate purchase price of approximately €16.0 million, subject to certain adjustments. The filing describes NeoVAD as a France-based value-added IT distributor specializing in cybersecurity, cloud services and virtualization solutions. Small bolt-ons like this extend a distributor's European footprint.

items.headline: TTM Technologies to acquire MKS's Ophir Optics for about $650M in cash
items.take: TTM Technologies said in its 8-K that it entered into a definitive agreement to acquire the Ophir Optics business from MKS Inc. for approximately $650 million in an all-cash transaction, subject to customary closing adjustments. The deal excludes MKS's Ophir Instruments laser characterization business, and closing is expected in the second quarter of 2027, subject to customary conditions including certain regulatory approvals.

items.headline: Francisco Partners completes Weave acquisition at $7.40 per share in cash
items.take: Weave said in its 8-K that Francisco Partners affiliates completed the acquisition on Oct. 26, 2026, with stockholders receiving $7.40 per share in cash, about $597.46 million in total. NYSE trading was suspended before the open on the closing date. Take-privates of mid-cap software names continue to close under private-equity ownership.

items.headline: Weave closes with new Hercules credit agreement: $190M term loan, $25M revolver
items.take: Under a credit agreement dated Oct. 26, 2026, Hercules Capital is administrative and collateral agent for a $190M initial term loan, a $25M initial delayed draw term loan and a $25M revolving facility, secured by substantially all assets. Weave's prior First-Citizens revolving line was repaid in full and terminated at closing. Private-credit lenders remain a source of financing in sponsor take-privates.

items.headline: CoStar signs agreement to acquire Vexcel Group for $730M in cash
items.take: CoStar Group's 8-K reports an Oct. 27, 2026 merger agreement to acquire Vexcel Group for $730 million in cash, subject to working capital and other post-closing adjustments. Closing requires HSR and certain foreign regulatory clearances and is not subject to CoStar stockholder approval or a financing condition. The agreement may be terminated if not consummated by July 27, 2027, subject to extension.

items.headline: Distribution Solutions Group's Lawson completes $145M Grade Eight acquisition
items.take: DSG's 8-K says Lawson Products completed the Grade Eight merger on Oct. 26, 2026, with a total purchase price of $145 million funded from DSG's existing $400 million revolving credit facility and available cash. Bolt-on deals funded on revolvers are a common route for industrial distributors.

items.headline: DSG filing: Eclipse take-private still pending stockholder approval
items.take: DSG's 8-K notes a July 15, 2026 merger agreement with Eclipse affiliates of LKCM Headwater Investments, which with affiliates owns approximately 78.5% of DSG common stock. The merger requires stockholder approval, a Schedule 13E-3 was filed Sept. 1, 2026, and the stock would no longer be listed on Nasdaq upon completion. The filing states DSG intends to file a definitive proxy statement.

items.headline: Fed H.15: 10-year Treasury yield 5.05% on Oct. 28, 30-year 5.37%
items.take: The Federal Reserve's H.15 release of Oct. 29 shows Treasury constant maturity yields on Oct. 28 of 4.67% at 2 years (4.70% on Oct. 27), 5.05% at 10 years (4.99%) and 5.37% at 30 years (5.30%). The 10-year yield was 6 basis points higher on the day while the 2-year was 3 basis points lower. The curve between the 2-year and 10-year steepened as a result.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board H.15 Selected Interest Rates

items.headline: 2s10s spread widens to 38 bp on Oct. 28 in Fed H.15 data
items.take: H.15 data show the 10-year Treasury constant maturity yield minus the 2-year at 38 basis points on Oct. 28 (5.05% less 4.67%), up from 29 basis points on Oct. 27 (4.99% less 4.70%). The effective federal funds rate was 3.88% on each day from Oct. 22 through Oct. 28. The 2-year yield sits 79 basis points above the policy-rate effective level, a gap AlphaGen reads as the market pricing a path of higher short-term rates than currently set.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board H.15 Selected Interest Rates

items.headline: Peoples Bancorp completes acquisition of Citizens National Corporation
items.take: Peoples Bancorp said the acquisition of Citizens National Corporation, parent of Citizens Bank of Kentucky, became effective at the close of business on October 30, 2026. Citizens shareholders received 2.10 Peoples shares plus $8.00 in cash per Citizens share, and Citizens had approximately $646 million in total assets at September 30, 2026. The release does not state a deal value; Peoples said it will convert the Citizens branches after the close of business on April 19, 2027.

items.headline: Kenvue Q3 net sales $3,886M vs $3,764M; diluted EPS $0.22 vs $0.21
items.take: Kenvue reported fiscal Q3 2026 net sales of $3,886 million versus $3,764 million a year earlier, up 3.2%, with organic sales growth of 2.9%. Diluted EPS was $0.22 versus $0.21, and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.29 versus $0.28. Pending-transaction costs tied to the Kimberly-Clark deal were $28 million in the quarter.

items.headline: Kenvue withholds guidance, cites pending Kimberly-Clark transaction
items.take: Kenvue said that due to the pending transaction with Kimberly-Clark it will not provide forward-looking guidance and will not host a quarterly conference call. The company expects pre-tax restructuring expenses and other charges of approximately $250 million in fiscal 2026. Pending-transaction and related costs were $60 million for the nine months.

items.headline: Eastman Chemical Q3 sales $2,385M vs $2,202M; diluted EPS $2.19 vs $0.60
items.take: Eastman reported Q3 2026 sales revenue of $2,385 million versus $2,202 million in Q3 2025, up 8.3%. GAAP diluted EPS was $2.19 versus $0.60, and adjusted EPS was $1.84 versus $1.14. The release revised the Q3 2025 income tax provision to correct an item, so the prior-year EPS comparison reflects that change.

items.headline: Eastman projects 2026 adjusted EPS of $6.00-$6.20, cash flow about $850M
items.take: Eastman said it projects full-year 2026 adjusted earnings per share between $6.00 and $6.20 and operating cash flow of approximately $850 million. The company said it expects sequential demand declines with normal seasonality and higher planned shutdown costs in Q4. It said it is on track for $125 million to $150 million of 2026 cost savings net of inflation.

items.headline: LyondellBasell Q3 sales $8,499M vs $7,727M; diluted EPS $2.32 vs $(2.77)
items.take: LyondellBasell reported Q3 2026 sales and other operating revenues of $8,499 million versus $7,727 million a year earlier, up 10.0%, and net income of $758 million versus a net loss of $890 million. Diluted EPS was $2.32 versus a loss of $2.77 per share. Capital spending was $303 million and dividends totaled $224 million in the quarter, so the swing to profit came alongside continued shareholder payouts.

items.headline: LyondellBasell sees Q4 operating rates of 85% N.A. O&P, 60% Europe O&P, 75% I&D
items.take: LyondellBasell said it expects fourth-quarter operating rates of 85% for North American O&P assets, 60% for European O&P assets and 75% for I&D assets, aligned with global demand and planned maintenance. The company expects normal seasonal demand patterns along with ongoing supply uncertainty. The gap between North American and European rates shows the regional split in its planned output.

items.headline: Magna Q3 sales $10,059M vs $10,462M; diluted EPS $1.44 vs $1.08
items.take: Magna reported Q3 2026 sales of $10,059 million versus $10,462 million a year earlier, adjusted EBIT of $683 million versus $613 million, and diluted EPS of $1.44 versus $1.08 (adjusted diluted EPS $1.83 versus $1.33). Adjusted EBIT margin was 6.8% versus 5.9%. Profit grew while sales fell, so the gain came from margin rather than volume.

items.headline: Magna narrows 2026 sales outlook to $41.2-$42.0B; declares $0.495 dividend
items.take: Magna's current 2026 total sales outlook is $41.2 to $42.0 billion versus the previous $41.3 to $42.5 billion, and its adjusted EBIT margin outlook is 6.3% to 6.5% versus 6.3% to 6.6%. The board declared a Q3 dividend of $0.495 per share, payable Nov. 27, 2026 to holders of record Nov. 13, and approved a new share repurchase program for up to about 25.8 million shares, subject to TSX approval. The top ends of both ranges came down while the company kept returning cash.

items.headline: CN Q3 revenues C$4,771M, up 15%; diluted EPS C$2.00 vs C$1.83
items.take: CN reported Q3 2026 revenues of C$4,771 million versus C$4,165 million, operating income of C$1,730 million versus C$1,606 million, and diluted EPS of C$2.00 versus C$1.83 (adjusted diluted EPS C$2.16). The operating ratio was 63.7% and the adjusted operating ratio 61.0%; adjustments included asset impairments and advisory costs related to rail consolidation matters. Adjusted results ran well ahead of reported ones, so the one-time items matter for reading the quarter.

items.headline: CN says 2026 adjusted EPS growth tracking toward upper end of mid-to-high single digits
items.take: CN said it continues to expect adjusted diluted EPS growth in the mid-to-high single-digit range and is tracking more towards the upper end, with low single-digit RTM growth assumed and a capital program of about C$2.8 billion. It declared a Q4 dividend of C$0.9150 per common share, payable Dec. 30, 2026. The guidance relies on an assumed WTI range of US$80 to US$110 per barrel for the balance of 2026.

items.headline: AbbVie Q3 diluted EPS $2.37 GAAP, $3.82 adjusted
items.take: AbbVie reported Q3 2026 diluted EPS of $2.37 on a GAAP basis and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.82. The release describes the GAAP figure as an increase of over 100.0 percent. Adjusted EPS excludes specified items, so the two figures are not directly comparable.

items.headline: BLS: Q3 employment costs up 0.8% in the quarter, 3.4% over the year
items.take: BLS reported civilian compensation costs rose 0.8% (seasonally adjusted) in the 3 months ending September 2026 and 3.4% (not seasonally adjusted) over 12 months, with wages and salaries up 3.1% and benefit costs up 3.9% over the year. Private-industry inflation-adjusted wages and salaries decreased 0.6% over the year. Benefit costs growing faster than wages shows employers' labor costs are rising more through benefits than pay.

items.headline: BEA: September PCE prices up 3.6% from a year ago; core up 3.1%
items.take: BEA reported the September PCE price index rose 0.5% from August and 3.6% from a year earlier, while excluding food and energy it rose 0.3% on the month and 3.1% over the year. Personal income increased $54.5 billion (0.2%) and consumer spending (PCE) increased $113.1 billion (0.5%). Spending outpacing income in a month of faster price gains is the combination to watch for household savings.
items.source_name: BEA Personal Income and Outlays, September 2026

items.headline: Exxon Q3 earnings $15.4B, $3.72 per share; plans $20B 2027 buybacks
items.take: ExxonMobil reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of $15.4 billion, or $3.72 per share (assuming dilution), with cash flow from operating activities of $25.7 billion and free cash flow of $19.1 billion. It declared a fourth-quarter dividend of $1.07 per share and announced 2027 share repurchases of $20 billion, assuming reasonable market conditions. The release compares the quarter with Q2 rather than Q3 2025, so the year-ago comparison is not stated in it.

items.headline: Chevron Q3 EPS $5.06 vs $1.82; total revenues and other income $67.8B
items.take: Chevron reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of $9.9 billion ($5.06 per share, diluted) versus $1.82 a year earlier, on total revenues and other income of $67,798 million versus $49,726 million (36.3% higher). Adjusted earnings were $10.4 billion ($5.28 per share). The board declared a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share, payable December 10, 2026.
items.source_name: Chevron Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Regeneron Q3 revenue $5.1B, up 36%; GAAP EPS $18.45 vs $13.62
items.take: Regeneron reported third-quarter 2026 revenues of $5,116 million versus $3,754 million, and GAAP diluted EPS of $18.45 versus $13.62 (non-GAAP $20.07 versus $11.83). Dupixent global net sales (recorded by Sanofi) rose 35% to $6.5 billion, and EYLEA HD U.S. net sales rose 62% to $699 million. Sanofi collaboration revenue of $2,724 million versus $1,617 million drove much of the revenue increase.

items.headline: Cboe Q3 diluted EPS $4.08 vs $2.85; lifts 2026 net revenue growth target
items.take: Cboe reported third-quarter 2026 total revenues of $1,358.8 million versus $1,141.7 million, net revenue of $712.2 million versus $605.5 million, and diluted EPS of $4.08 versus $2.85. It now expects 2026 organic total net revenue growth in the 'high teens' range, up from prior guidance of 'mid to high teens'. Net revenue grew 17.6% year over year, per our calculation.
items.source_name: Cboe Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC Form 8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Colgate Q3 net sales $5,369M vs $5,131M; diluted EPS $0.94 vs $0.91
items.take: Colgate-Palmolive reported third-quarter 2026 net sales of $5,369 million versus $5,131 million (4.6% higher by our calculation) and GAAP diluted EPS of $0.94 versus $0.91. Sales grew faster than per-share earnings, which rose 3.3%.

items.headline: General Dynamics Q3 operating earnings $1.5B; $4.49 per diluted share
items.take: General Dynamics reported third-quarter 2026 operating earnings of $1.5 billion and $4.49 per diluted share, according to the company's release dated Oct. 30, 2026. Defense contractors' quarterly results are worth reading alongside backlog and cash flow disclosures in the full release.

items.headline: Intel Q3 revenue $16.5B, up 21%; GAAP EPS $0.60 vs $0.90
items.take: Intel reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $16.5 billion, up 21% year-over-year, and GAAP diluted EPS attributable to Intel of $0.60 versus $0.90 a year earlier. Data Center and AI revenue was $7.3 billion, up 78%. Revenue growth alongside lower GAAP EPS means the year-over-year comparison depends on which earnings basis is used.

items.headline: Intel forecasts Q4 2026 revenue of $15.0B to $16.0B
items.take: Intel said it is forecasting fourth-quarter 2026 revenue of $15.0 billion to $16.0 billion. Third-quarter revenue was $16.5 billion, so the range sits below the quarter just reported. The release gives a quarterly range rather than a full-year revenue outlook.

items.headline: Reddit Q3 revenue $895M, up 53%; diluted EPS $1.40 vs $0.80
items.take: Reddit said total revenue increased 53% year-over-year to $895 million in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, with ad revenue up 54% to $847 million. Diluted EPS was $1.40 versus $0.80. Ad revenue made up the large majority of the total, so the quarter tracks advertising demand.

items.headline: Reddit guides Q4 revenue $1,000M-$1,030M, adj. EBITDA $480M-$510M
items.take: Reddit gave fourth-quarter revenue guidance in the range of $1,000 million to $1,030 million and Adjusted EBITDA in the range of $480 million to $510 million. The release does not include full-year guidance. Q3 revenue was $895 million, so the range sits above the quarter just reported.

items.headline: Twilio Q3 revenue $1.56B, up 20%; GAAP diluted EPS $1.00 vs $0.23
items.take: Twilio reported revenue of $1.56 billion, up 20% reported and 16% organic year-over-year, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. GAAP diluted net income per share was $1.00 versus $0.23 in Q3 2025. The gap between reported and organic growth shows part of the increase came from outside organic activity.

items.headline: Twilio raises 2026 outlook: reported growth 20%, organic 15%
items.take: Twilio raised its full-year 2026 reported revenue growth outlook to 20% from 18% to 18.5%, and organic growth to 15% from 13% to 13.5%. It initiated fourth-quarter revenue of $1.595 billion to $1.605 billion. Both full-year figures moved up by roughly two points.

items.headline: Lilly Q3 revenue $24.4B, up 39%; EPS $7.22 vs $6.21
items.take: Lilly reported Q3 2026 worldwide revenue of $24.4 billion, an increase of 39% from Q3 2025, driven by a 53% increase in volume partially offset by a 15% decrease in realized prices. Reported EPS was $7.22 versus $6.21, and non-GAAP EPS was $7.48 versus $7.02; both periods included acquired IPR&D charges, $4.57 per share in Q3 2026 and $0.71 in Q3 2025. The volume-versus-price split shows the growth came from selling more product rather than from higher prices.
items.source_name: Eli Lilly Q3 2026 earnings release (PR Newswire)

items.headline: Lilly lifts 2026 revenue guidance midpoint $5.5B to $91.0-$92.0B
items.take: Lilly said it increased the midpoint of its 2026 full-year revenue guidance by $5.5 billion to a range of $91.0 billion to $92.0 billion. It gave an updated non-GAAP EPS range of $35.00 to $36.00. The release also lists Q3 non-GAAP net income of $6.7 billion, so the revenue guide and the EPS guide are being set on different bases and should be read separately.
items.source_name: Eli Lilly Q3 2026 earnings release (PR Newswire)

items.headline: Fannie Mae Q3 net income $4,177M vs $3,859M; net worth $119.6B
items.take: Fannie Mae reported Q3 2026 net income of $4,177 million versus $3,859 million a year earlier, and net worth of $119,637 million at Sept. 30, 2026. The release states actual available CET1 capital was a deficit of $30 billion, and single-family conventional acquisition volume was $88.3 billion versus $111.2 billion in Q2. Net income rose about 8% year over year, but the capital deficit shows the conservatorship rebuild remains a long way from the required levels.

items.headline: Freddie Mac Q3 net income $3,235M vs $2,773M; net worth $81.0B
items.take: Freddie Mac reported Q3 2026 net income of $3,235 million versus $2,773 million in Q3 2025 and comprehensive income of $3,206 million, with net worth of $80,975 million at Sept. 30, 2026. The release says no dividend was paid to Treasury on the senior preferred stock in September 2026 because the company has not yet built enough capital to meet required levels and buffers. Net income rose about 17% year over year while single-family acquisition volume was $98 billion versus $99 billion.
items.source_name: Freddie Mac Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Smurfit Westrock Q3 net sales $8,161M; adj. EBITDA $1,205M; FY view ~$4.7B
items.take: Smurfit Westrock reported Q3 2026 net sales of $8,161 million, net income of $219 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $1,205 million, a 14.8% margin. The company estimates full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $4.7 billion and expects about $700 million of additional freight and energy costs in 2026. The quarterly dividend is $0.4523 per share, payable Dec. 10 to holders of record Nov. 13.

items.headline: Landstar Q3 revenue $1,511.8M vs $1,205.4M; EPS $1.42 vs $0.56
items.take: Landstar reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1,511.8 million versus $1,205.4 million, net income of $48.0 million versus $19.4 million, and EPS of $1.42 versus $0.56. The year-earlier quarter included a $30.1 million non-cash impairment charge. Total loads were 516,110 versus 501,230, and the company repurchased 232,645 shares for $41.4 million in the quarter.

items.headline: BLS: jobs report Nov. 6, CPI Nov. 10, PPI Nov. 13 on November schedule
items.take: BLS's November schedule lists JOLTS for September on Tuesday, Nov. 3 at 10:00 a.m. ET, Productivity and Costs on Nov. 5, the October Employment Situation on Friday, Nov. 6 at 8:30 a.m., the October CPI on Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 8:30 a.m., and the October PPI on Friday, Nov. 13. Nov. 11 is Veterans Day with no release listed. Those readings land after the Fed's Oct. 28 meeting, so they are the next official labor and price data points.
items.source_name: BLS Schedule of Selected Releases for November 2026

items.headline: Treasury tentative schedule: 3-yr Nov. 9, 10-yr reopening Nov. 10, 30-yr Nov. 12
